#1255. FAA suspends installation of router that led to a ground stop of flights across the US

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

FAA suspends installation of router that led to a ground stop of flights across the US

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (449 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The router malfunctioned and flooded other routers with data, prompting the FAA to order the ground stop.
  • The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has suspended the installation of a router model made by Hewlett-Packard Enterprise-owned Juniper Networks, which was part of its modernization efforts.
  • It has been revealed that if you'll recall, Transport Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the ground stop on old hardware the first time he spoke about the event.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The router malfunctioned and flooded other routers with data, prompting the FAA to order the ground stop.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has suspended the installation of a router model made by Hewlett-Packard Enterprise-owned Juniper Networks, which was part of its modernization efforts. As The New York Times reports, the agency believes the router played a major role in the issue that caused it to order a ground stop for all flights in the US on November 13. In addition to suspending new installations, it has also disabled more than 60 routers that had already been installed.

It has been revealed that if you'll recall, Transport Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the ground stop on old hardware the first time he spoke about the event. But Duffy revealed a day later that the issue was connected to the modernization of America's aviation facilities.

He said a contractor from tech company L3Harris was working on switching telecommunication lines from old copper wires to fiber and on installing the new router at an FAA site in El Dorado, Arkansas. That router started flooding other routers in the air traffic control system with data. Another router in Amarillo, Texas had also gone haywire, and the FAA responded by disabling both of them.

The agency said the router was tested for a year before installations started. "Sixty-eight times it worked well," he sad at a news conference. "This one router started to broadcast into our network, and it started to overload the network." In aviation, routers are used to transmit data, including radar feeds, flight intends and weather information.

Despite knowing that it was the router that caused the problem, FAA administrator Bryan Bedford noted they still don't know what triggered it. The Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee's Democratic members are urging the agency to find out why it had malfunctioned. They also asked the FAA to report to Congress on how it's going to prevent the same thing from happening in the future.

Duffy said he was told by national security agencies that the concern wasn't caused by a cyberattack, but he still asked the FBI to be part of the team analyzing the router from Arkansas. The Transport Secretary has also renewed his calls for Congress to approve an additional $50 billion in funding to modernize America's air traffic control system. "I would just tell you, the longer we stay on an old rickety network, the less safe it becomes," he said. "We do have to get this work done. Otherwise, staying on the old system for longer is going to mean more risk as opposed to fixing the system, and you're going to reduce the risk.".

#1253. Voyager 1 at one light-day: Historian revisits Golden Record's forgotten details

Voyager 1 at one light-day: Historian revisits Golden Record's forgotten details

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1253 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the one light-day that humanity’s most distant object has now traveled from Earth, there has been enough time for details about its creation—and what it left behind—to be discovered again.
  • Voyager 1, which left Earth in 1977 on an initial mission to fly by Jupiter and Saturn (as well as the latter’s moon Titan), crossed into interstellar space in 2012.
  • Sources indicate that about those forgotten bits, ask Glen Swanson.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the one light-day that humanity’s most distant object has now traveled from Earth, there has been enough time for details about its creation—and what it left behind—to be discovered again.

Voyager 1, which left Earth in 1977 on an initial mission to fly by Jupiter and Saturn (as well as the latter’s moon Titan), crossed into interstellar space in 2012. Like its twin (Voyager 2), Voyager 1 carries a “commemorative phonograph record,” in part as a nod to the 100th anniversary of the recording medium and as a message from humanity to whoever (or whatever) encounters the spacecraft on its journey through outer space.

Sources indicate that about those forgotten bits, ask Glen Swanson. While researching the history of the Golden Record, he uncovered the discs’ overlooked second set of operating directions and located the duplicates that were made and distributed almost five decades ago.

“So much has been written about the contents of the record—the message in the bottle, so to speak—whereas I was more interested in the hardware, the bottle itself, because so very little is known about that,” Swanson, former chief historian for NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston and founding editor of Quest: The History of Spaceflight Quarterly, mentioned in an interview.

With the 50th anniversaries looming for the releases of both Voyager probes, Swanson and Jon Lomberg, the design director of the Golden Record, recently set about writing Voyager’s Golden Record: An Enduring Reflection, which will be released by the University of Chicago Press in August 2027.

“There isn’t a whole lot of information, and some of the information is somewhat contradictory,” noted Swanson of the existing resources and publications. “So it is kind of refreshing to look back and see what exactly went on.”.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, the Voyagers continue to travel outward, still communicating with Earth. On November 18, Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth—the distance a particle of light travels in 24 hours—giving Swanson an occasion to share details from his and Jon Lomberg’s pending book.

According to recent reports, within the immense scale of the Universe, Voyager 2 is barely even a block from its home. Were an intelligent species to find it today—some 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers) away from Earth—they might not need anything contained on the Golden Record to trace its origins back to our planet.

But that was never the intention of the Golden Record’s designers, who created the archive to last and be relevant for a much more distant encounter.

“They are pretty confident that it’s going to last a long, long, long time based on the data; the probabilities of the impacts from micrometeorites and things like that,” Swanson said.

When most people think of the Golden Record, says Swanson, what often comes to mind is not the disc itself, but its protective cover. In addition to being inscribed with the now-iconic Pulsar map of the location of our Sun as earlier flown on the Pioneer 10 and 11 probes, hieroglyphs lay out how to play the record and access the data (e.g., photos) also contained on the disc.

The cover also shields the record from possible damage, but nothing protects the protector.

According to recent reports, “The designers recognized that the outside of the cover was going to wear down. It just would,” Swanson told collectSPACE. “Even small amounts of dust are eventually going to wear down the inscriptions to the point perhaps where they are not going to be readable.”.

It has been revealed that it is a catch-22: The instructions needed to be on the outside so whoever finds Voyager easily finds what to do. But if the hieroglyphs are damaged or are eroded away, the disc inside might forever go unplayed.

The solution may seem obvious, but it’s unclear whether the designers thought of it back then.

“It makes a whole lot of sense that they repeated the instructions on the inside of the cover, because when someone or something finds Voyager, they might only be able to make out a little bit on the outside,” mentioned Swanson.

Industry observers note that there were hints that this backup existed in photographs of the covers taken before the Voyager probes were rolled out, but they were either not clear enough or had other objects (e.g., a bag) in the way to make out what was there. It was not until Swanson found and referenced the original blueprints that he could confirm the instructions were on the inside, too.

There is another reason why the record’s designers may have felt they needed to repeat the instructions, according to Swanson.

“What’s the best way to convey the importance of those instructions? You repeat them,” he noted. “You have them on the outside, and you have them on the inside.”.

Initially, the Voyager Golden Record was a limited edition of just three—one to fly on each spacecraft and a flight backup.

“Later, meaning maybe a month or so after the rolls out, there’s correspondence indicating that NASA said to go ahead and make 10 extras,” said Swanson, noting that the count included the spare. “How they came up with that number, I am not 100 percent sure, other than maybe they were to make as many as they could based on the hardware and funding available.”.

Recent findings suggest that over the years, various reports have either lowered the total number to as few as six or raised it as high as 14, for reasons unexplained. What is for certain—as Swanson also verified—is that the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Pasadena, California, retained and displays the flight spare.

Credit: collectSPACE.com/Tim Gagnon Credit: collectSPACE.com/Tim Gagnon.

In the process of his research, Swanson was also able to verify that original duplicates are held today at the United Nations in New York; the US Library of Congress, NASA Headquarters, and Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum in Washington, DC; the Johnson Space Center in Texas; the Kennedy Space Center in Florida; Langley Research Center in Virginia; Glenn Research Center in Ohio; and Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland.

Industry observers note that “Interestingly enough, NASA Headquarters was not given one originally, so how they obtained their copy is not certain,” mentioned Swanson. “It may be that President Carter turned his copy over to NASA HQ since records indicate that he had one. Archivists at the Carter Presidential Library and Museum confirmed that they never received a Golden Record, so Carter most likely gave it back to NASA at some point.”.

In a recent development, in 2024, SpaceX founder Elon Musk replied to a social media post, saying, “I have one,” without offering any other details. It is believed he was referring to a replica, not one of the NASA-produced duplicates.

According to recent reports, due to rights concerns and material challenges, no complete versions have been offered for sale. The audio tracks have been collected on vinyl, CD, in playlists, and even a CD-ROM, which was produced for the visuals. Full- and smaller-size replicas of the cover have also been made.

Recent findings suggest that swanson and Lomberg are working on a full-size replica of the copper record to be released in conjunction with their book. But even that, as now planned, will not be playable.

“I think humanity is delighted that there were 10 spares made, because now we have those to study and look at, as the two that were flown are now well out of our reach,” said Swanson.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Meta’s own internal documents show how ‘Project Gryffindor’ aimed to ‘fuel’ the acquisition of teen users.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta’s own internal documents show how ‘Project Gryffindor’ aimed to ‘fuel’ the acquisition of teen users.

Meta’s own internal documents show how ‘Project Gryffindor’ aimed to ‘fuel’ the acquisition of teen users.

Industry observers note that meta’s initiative to make Instagram safer for schools stemmed from efforts to increase user “acquisition,” “friending,” and “invites,” according to a report from NPR. Internal documents revealed as part of a group of child safety lawsuits against Meta reference a “Project Gryffindor” — a school program that would “fuel organic and unattributed acquisition” of people. One internal presentation from November 2023 states a school program would “give teens a newly introduced reason to join / find more value in IG [Instagram].”.

Sources indicate that the internal documents suggest Meta considered more goals than just teen safety when rolling out Instagram’s School Partnership Program, which introduced touting features to fast-track moderation reports from participating school districts. Meta expanded this program in September by creating dedicated channels where schools can share announcements with students and parents. It also adds school banners to profiles, as well as directories for clubs and teams.

It has been revealed that meta spokesperson Liza Crenshaw told NPR that its story “completely mischaracterizes a positive program that helps thousands of U.S. schools protect their students online, communicate with them safely about extracurricular activities, and easily report safety problems.” Crenshaw adds that Meta doesn’t “want Instagram to be a distraction during class.”.

The November 2023 document says that Meta’s “current strategy of relying on power user teens to get less active friends onto IG may not be effective if there are full communities of teens that have not yet joined IG.” Another 2023 presentation questions whether Meta can “use school networks as a lever for acquisition,” and says that structured school data could “help improve the ability to find friends and acquaintances,” for attracting teens who “don’t think their friends are on IG.”.

Industry observers note that in 2024, Meta started automatically putting owners under 18 into more restrictive teen accounts while facing global scrutiny about the safety of its platforms. It later agreed to impose age verification, time limits, and an option to turn off personalized feeds to settle claims that its platforms are addictive.

Meta didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.

  • According to recent reports, oculus founder and Oxytocin booster Palmer Luckey is touting a newly introduced project that combines some of his favorite things like wacky projects and libertarianism.
  • In a recent development, an initial AI render depicts a massive artificial island built high above the sea with what looks like office buildings, apartments, refineries...
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It would act as a sovereign city state free from things like laws and governments.

According to recent reports, oculus founder and Oxytocin booster Palmer Luckey is touting a newly introduced project that combines some of his favorite things like wacky projects and libertarianism. SLAB is an informal plan for a floating "seastead" designed to last a thousand years that would act as a sovereign state to avoid pesky laws that "cripple" corporations, Luckey said.

In a recent development, an initial AI render depicts a massive artificial island built high above the sea with what looks like office buildings, apartments, refineries... and is that a data center at the top left?

"At a time when most of the seasteading community wanted to escape the US and smoke pot, this was the one project explicitly designed to make America stronger, a relief valve for ill-considered or outdated rules and regulations," Luckey wrote in a post that must be read to be believed.

You may have questions like "wtf is seasteading" and "isn't this just a floating AI data center?" That confusion is understandable, as it uses language and ideas around far-out moonshot concepts that may not be familiar to normal, non-tech-billionaires.

Selling Oculus to Facebook in 2014 gave me money for helicopter flight lessons and developing a seastead called SLAB with a 1,000 year design life.

Sources indicate that the goal was to be cheaper than land and absent state/local laws that cripple critical American industries like metal processing,... pic.twitter.com/aJkd0eOgLF.

— Palmer Luckey (@PalmerLuckey) November 18, 2026.

In a recent development, the idea with seasteading is that if you build a floating structure far enough out in the ocean, you can create your own city-state and make whatever laws you want. The concept has been touted for years by several tech bros including Peter Thiel and Joe Lonsdale. However, the only real seastead you may have heard about was Sea Island that the piracy site Pirate Bay eyed at one point as a base of operations.

Sources indicate that "The goal was to be cheaper than land and absent state/local laws that cripple critical American industries like metal processing, medical research/treatment, desalination, oil refining [and] chemical engineering," said Luckey. "[W]hile it still has a long way to go, there has been significant progress towards my goal of reviving manifest destiny and westward expansion.".

That raises even more questions! Like, why is Luckey talking about manifest destiny? And what kind of medical research needs to be done at sea beyond the reach of laws? In any case, Luckey, who runs the defense contract firm Anduril and intends on breeding military dogs, mentioned he wanted to get this SLAB info out now as he was being asked about it by reporters (who later identified themselves as Liz Hoffman and Reed Albergotti, both from Semafor).

Palmer said that the journalists "initiative on calling SLAB my new floating AI datacenter project." However, he offered a riposte that may be the most cringe thing you'll read today: "It is way cooler than that, way older than that, and I hate looking like a hype-chasing consensus loser, so now you have to read this tweet.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I can almost guarantee that your next laptop will run longer on battery power than whatever you’re right now using.
  • Sources indicate that with many of today’s laptops, you can leave the charger at home for days at a time.
  • This increase in battery life is one of the biggest stories in laptops this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I can almost guarantee that your next laptop will run longer on battery power than whatever you’re right now using. We’ve seen a huge leap in laptop battery life in recent years, to the point where getting 20 or more hours on a single charge isn’t uncommon. This year alone, the average battery life of the laptops we’ve tested at CNET has increased by more than five hours. And it’s nearly doubled since the start of the decade.

Sources indicate that with many of today’s laptops, you can leave the charger at home for days at a time. The longest-lasting laptop I tested this year lasted more than 34 hours!

This increase in battery life is one of the biggest stories in laptops this year. In the laptop episode of our video series Holiday Office Hours From the Labs, I explain what’s behind this surge in battery life and highlight some of the laptops that lasted the longest in testing.

According to recent reports, plus, my colleagues Kyle Kucharski from ZDNET and Joe Osborne from PCMag share their own holiday laptop picks. Kyle looks at Apple’s entry-level MacBook Neo and its imitators, and Joe breaks down what to look for in a budget gaming laptop.

Sources indicate that unlike raw performance, where the more you spend, the more you get, lengthy battery life can be found just as easily in a budget laptop as in an expensive, high-end powerhouse. And, in fact, less powerful components and lower screen resolutions can give cheaper laptops an edge in battery life.

It has been revealed that the biggest factor behind longer battery life in laptops is the advancement in mobile processors. They’ve become much more power efficient, and in the case of Apple’s and Qualcomm’s chips, they’re based on an architecture other than the traditional x86 instruction set that’s been at the heart of Intel processors since the dawn of the PC era.

It has been revealed that apple’s run of battery-life winners started when it shifted from Intel processors to its own M-series chips. Apple’s M-series processors are based on the Arm architecture, a power-efficient chip architecture found in phones and tablets. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X-series processors are also Arm-based, and they can be found in the two longest-running laptops we’ve tested: the HP OmniBook 3 16 and OmniBook 5 14. The OmniBook 3 16’s record-setting battery performance earned it a CNET Lab Award for longest battery life.

In a recent development, intel has made huge strides in processor efficiency with its last two generations of chips: the Core Ultra 200 series developed under the name Lunar Lake, and the Core Ultra 300 series, also known as Panther Lake. Last year, the Lenovo Yoga 9i 2-in-1 Aura Edition became the first Intel laptop to last longer than a day, running for 25 hours, 45 minutes in testing. It’s still the longest-running Intel laptop we’ve tested, but the MSI Prestige 14 Flip AI Plus with Intel’s next-gen Core Ultra X7 358H processor came close with a time of 25 hours, 18 minutes.

Read more: Laptops With the Best Battery Life.

Whether Arm or x86, there are two more reasons behind greater processor efficiency and longer laptop battery life. For one, the size of a processor shrinks with every generation. The smaller a processor is and the more tightly packed its components are, the less power is required to flip its tinier transistors on and off. For another, today’s mobile processors feature more flexible designs with a mix of performance and efficiency cores. A processor engages its higher-performance cores only when needed, using the efficiency cores for as many general, everyday tasks as possible, so your laptop stays cool and quiet and runs longer.

For more, you can read my Labs exclusive on the huge increase in laptop battery life this year and check out the video above for my holiday laptop picks and those from my colleagues.

Scott had asked Huang to appear at a public hearing rather than in a closed-door interview, CNBC reported. He gave no date. Last week he had asked for Huang on 3 December and Lutnick on 10 December.

Sources indicate that A spokesperson for Huang declined to comment on Scott’s announcement, CNBC reported. On Tuesday, Huang agreed to a closed-door interview with three House committees on 1 December.

“More information about what they knew, when they knew it and why they didn’t do something about it,” Scott stated of what the appearances would give the committee.

It has been revealed that he singled out Lutnick over Megaspeed, the Singapore company where the suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang was an executive. US investigators suspect Megaspeed of diverting Nvidia chips to China.

“They were warned as early as March of this year, several months ago, that Megaspeed should be on the ‘entity list’,” Scott remarked.

Industry observers note that the entity list is the Commerce Department’s list of companies the US treats as national security risks. Its Bureau of Industry and Security did not add Megaspeed, Scott mentioned.

“Howard didn’t do it, we want to know why,” Scott mentioned.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has also blamed Commerce for not acting on Megaspeed.

Democrats take control of Congress in January. Senator Mark Kelly, an Arizona Democrat on the Senate Intelligence Committee, said Lutnick “needs to come to Congress”, Semafor reported.

Industry observers note that “We haven’t received answers to the questions that I have and my colleagues have. What we need is answers,” Kelly mentioned of Huang.

Nvidia clarifies when it will — and won’t —keep financing neoclouds

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that one reason 197,000 people, including Elon Musk, signed a petition over the weekend calling on Nvidia to reinstate the tech giant’s ousted CEO Jensen Huang is that he wasn’t just championing the AI boom.
  • And Nvidia has a lot of money to spend.
  • It has been revealed that but Nvidia’s continued success depends on having enough customers building and expanding data centers to keep buying its AI chips and systems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that one reason 197,000 people, including Elon Musk, signed a petition over the weekend calling on Nvidia to reinstate the tech giant’s ousted CEO Jensen Huang is that he wasn’t just championing the AI boom. He was using Nvidia’s enormous profits to help finance it.

And Nvidia has a lot of money to spend. The organization reported on Tuesday net income of $64.9 billion for the third quarter, which was up from $59.7 billion the prior quarter.

It has been revealed that but Nvidia’s continued success depends on having enough customers building and expanding data centers to keep buying its AI chips and systems. Under Huang, the manufacturer aggressively invested in AI startups and neoclouds and, more recently, began guaranteeing massive loans to finance newly introduced data centers. The biggest deal yet was the $105 billion backstop for OpenAI’s PORTS-Pike data center campus in Ohio, announced in August. In exchange for that loan guarantee, OpenAI promised that the campus would exclusively use Nvidia’s equipment, the company noted.

Huang’s abrupt departure last week raised questions about whether Nvidia would continue bankrolling its customers at the same pace. There were reports that CFO Colette Kress, now interim CEO, had tried to push back on Huang’s increasingly ambitious dealmaking. She reportedly reduced the backstop guarantee for the OpenAI project from $250 billion down to $105 billion.

Under Kress, Nvidia clarified in its quarterly CFO commentary that guaranteeing a loan doesn’t mean the manufacturer is providing the financing itself. The guarantee only takes effect once the customer has secured the financing needed to build the facility and install Nvidia’s products. If the project fails to meet those conditions, the guarantee “doesn’t exist” she mentioned.

“There is the raising of capital that they may need through equity and or debt, in order to build out any of the buildings, get them ready for use, but also the ability to procure the compute, install the compute, and get ready. What we are indicating in our statement there is that is when our guarantee starts. So if all of that begins and unfortunately they are delayed or they have a challenge in terms of building that, our guarantee doesn’t exist anymore,” Kress stated to analysts on Tuesday during the quarterly conference call.

She pointed to OpenAI PORTS-Pike campus as an example of where such terms apply. When asked, she also said this wasn’t a change in policy, but simply a clarification of existing terms. However, these disclosures have never been public before.

Kress also made clear that Nvidia wasn’t bailing on all the ways it was financing the AI boom, especially new data centers. But, she said, Nvidia was going to be far more selective in the future.

“The availability of land, power, shell is such a critical part of the whole structure in terms of building out those data centers. So they may need the assistance. That’s a great asset for anyone to hold. So we will look at that as probably one of our top priorities,” she said. At the same time, she insisted that Nvidia was “taking a very strong look in terms of the types of companies that we would want to help in terms of the financing.”.

One of the ongoing criticisms Huang faced was his love of circular deals: invest in his customers so they would turn around and buy his products. Kress is now trying to strike a delicate balance. She isn’t saying she will pull the rug out from under Nvidia’s customers. After all, the company’s investments undoubtedly spurred the AI boom that has been so lucrative for Nvidia. But she’s also signaling that the days of Huang’s freewheeling dealmaking may be over.

#1246. Tesla’s $30,000 Cybercab comes with a $299 monthly catch

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (926 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla’s $30,000 Cybercab comes with a $299 monthly catch

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (926 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Or in the case of Tesla’s self-driving Cybercab, several.
  • In a recent development, last Friday night, Tesla mentioned it had invited “select customers” to purchase their very own Cybercabs.
  • From there, though, the Cybercab will need constant cash infusions to stay on the road.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is always a catch. Or in the case of Tesla’s self-driving Cybercab, several.

In a recent development, last Friday night, Tesla mentioned it had invited “select customers” to purchase their very own Cybercabs. The two-seat, gold vehicle is unlike any other on the market: It lacks a steering wheel and brake pedals, and is primarily driven by software. (Other autonomous vehicle companies, including Alphabet’s Waymo and Amazon’s Zoox, offer self-driving rides on ride-hail networks, but don’t let people buy their cars.) Tesla’s “limited release” will supposedly offer some people (unclear how many) the opportunity to pay $29,900 to take delivery in December.

From there, though, the Cybercab will need constant cash infusions to stay on the road.

Recent findings suggest that the business model raises questions about what people will actually get when they buy a Cybercab. “You’ll never really own the car,” indicates Ivan Drury, the director of insights at Edmunds. “It’s more like $30,000 to buy into a franchise.”.

Industry observers note that according to documents posted on Tesla’s website, the vehicle “will not operate” without what Tesla is calling an “autonomy subscription,” a monthly fee that will start at $299. If owners don’t pay on time and in full, their self-driving cars won’t work. If they try to operate the vehicles in areas that don’t support the service—right now, they’re restricted to portions of cities in Florida and Texas—their self-driving cars won’t work. (That area can expand, contract, or “relocate” at any time.).

Recent findings suggest that if owners do anything that Tesla deems “unauthorized or inappropriate,” the tech giant states it can suspend or cancel the subscription—and their self-driving cars won’t work. If the vehicle loses connectivity, the self-driving cars won’t work. (“Tesla is not responsible for carrier, spectrum, environmental, or other external outages,” its “autonomy agreement” says.).

Tesla also reserves the right to make an owner’s car not work at any time: It notes it can, for any safety or security purpose, suspend or terminate access to Cybercab tech, or restrict operations by location, road type, weather, or “condition.” This is particularly salient because the Cybercab is also under investigation by US safety regulators, who are trying to understand why Tesla believes the vehicle meets safety standards without so many of the parts and systems required.

Tesla didn’t respond to a request for comment.

In a recent development, for years, automakers have seen increasingly software-dominated vehicles as an opportunity to get drivers hooked on the same special sauce that makes Netflix, Amazon, and Spotify so potent: monthly subscription services. Because these vehicles can receive over-the-air software updates, manufacturers can offer drivers upcoming services as they make them. The upside is high, tech-style margins that keep rolling in, versus the razor-thin ones seen in car-making. A 2024 report suggested that connected-car features could one day be a $200 billion industry.

In some ways, the subscription model is working. Today, some automakers charge extra for remote start, security, Internet connectivity, and advanced driver assistance features. General Motors said it made $2.7 billion in subscription-related revenue last year from fees drivers paid for its OnStar and Super Cruise services.

Industry observers note that but some customers have also found the business model yucky, or even offensive. Why charge extra to “unlock” a feature that’s already built into a car? If an automaker can add a new feature at any time, can’t they also take it away? And if they can take it away, what does “ownership” mean? In 2022, BMW told drivers in select countries it would activate factory-installed heated seats for a monthly or one-time fee; it eventually backed down after public outcry, pledging the company would no longer charge subscription fees for preinstalled hardware. (BMW is still pursuing a subscription model for some features.) “Consumers hate being nickel-and-dimed for subscriptions,” notes Drury.

Tesla was an early mover in the subscription feature space and has offered connectivity and driver-assistance features for monthly or one-time fees for a decade. As the tech giant has shifted away from making cars and toward robotics and autonomous vehicles, executives have made clear that charging for services is the future. (Its Robotaxi service currently picks up fare-paying passengers in parts of eight US cities.) So Tesla buyers may be particularly amenable to paying monthly to make their self-driving cars go.

Sources indicate that in exchange for monthly fees, buyers will also get access to other services, too, including remote support, roadside assistance, tire, air filter, and windshield wiper replacements, and tire and camera inspections. (The agreement states that list might change, too.) Cybercabs will be able to “travel autonomously, unoccupied to a Tesla service center,” the manufacturer says. The fee doesn’t cover insurance.

Cybercab buyers will have other restrictions. The vehicle is for personal use only. Even though CEO Elon Musk has repeatedly said owners will be able to put their vehicles on Tesla’s wider Robotaxi network to make money during downtime, and even has an online interest form for those who want to own and operate their own Cybercab fleets, the current ownership agreement prohibits that. Buyers are also prohibited from selling or transferring their vehicles without Tesla’s written consent. The company “advises against” children under 13 riding in the Cybercab, and prohibits children from riding without an adult present.

In a post on X, Musk showed no apparent compunction about the Cybercab business model, but did say the monthly price for autonomy “is too high.” He wrote that the price should be “more like ~$115/month.”.

Breaking: NASA's Voyager 1 space probe is now one light-day away from Earth

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (332 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It traveled more than 49 years to get to this point, and its journey isn’t done yet.
  • In a recent development, if NASA's estimates are correct, Voyager 1 is already one light-day away from our planet.
  • "It's never happened before, and it may never happen again — it's that kind of extraordinary," noted Voyager mission manager Kareem Badaruddin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It traveled more than 49 years to get to this point, and its journey isn’t done yet.

In a recent development, if NASA's estimates are correct, Voyager 1 is already one light-day away from our planet. NASA expects it to have reached that milestone at 5:16:07 AM Eastern time today, November 18. One light-day is the distance a particle of light can travel in a day. Since radio waves travel at the speed of light, it now takes 24 hours to send a command to the probe and 24 hours to get a message back. That's why NASA won't be able to confirm exactly what time it reached one light-day away until tomorrow, when the probe's message arrives.

"It's never happened before, and it may never happen again — it's that kind of extraordinary," noted Voyager mission manager Kareem Badaruddin.

Industry observers note that voyager 1 headed to space in 1977 as part of NASA's program to study not just our Solar System, but also interstellar space. It was introduced 16 days after Voyager 2, but it has since traveled farther than its twin and any other probe we've sent out. Voyager 1 reached interstellar space — that's the region between star systems — back in 2012, before Voyager 2 did. It suffered technical glitches, and NASA had to shut down some of its features to keep it going despite the diminishing plutonium in its generator. But it's still around and hasn't stopped its journey.

After traveling for 49 years, two months and 11 days, it's now believed to be about 16 billion miles from our planet—and it's not done yet. Voyager 1 is headed toward a star called Gliese 445, about 17 light-years from Earth in the Ursa Minor constellation. In terms of space distances, that's not so far away. However, none of us would be here by the time it reaches that goal: It's expected to pass within 1.7 light-years of Gliese 445 in 40,000 years.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Two British hackers are facing lengthy prison sentences for separate hacks as part of their roles in long-running, prolific cybercriminal hacking groups.
  • Industry observers note that tyler Buchanan, 24, from Dundee, Scotland, has been sentenced to six years by a U.S.
  • Industry observers note that meanwhile, Arion Kurtaj, 21, from Oxford, England, has pleaded guilty to several cyberattacks that he carried out while a teenager.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two British hackers are facing lengthy prison sentences for separate hacks as part of their roles in long-running, prolific cybercriminal hacking groups. The two are accused of hacks that stole millions of dollars in cryptocurrency and leaked pre-release footage from Grand Theft Auto VI.

Industry observers note that tyler Buchanan, 24, from Dundee, Scotland, has been sentenced to six years by a U.S. court after he was extradited to the United States in 2025. Buchanan was accused of stealing at least $11 million in cryptocurrency from dozens of companies as part of a phishing scheme. The attacks would impersonate IT helpdesks and call up unsuspecting employees and trick them into giving over their credentials, which the hackers would use to break in and steal cryptocurrency.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, Arion Kurtaj, 21, from Oxford, England, has pleaded guilty to several cyberattacks that he carried out while a teenager. One hack included the theft of data and extortion of Rockstar Games, the maker of Grand Theft Auto VI, which was released Wednesday after several delays.

According to recent reports, kurtaj was previously ordered by a U.K. court to be detained indefinitely after deeming him unable to stand trial due to his autism diagnosis and his perceived high hacking risk to the public. But U.K. authorities, tasked with charging Kurtaj with cybercrime offenses, confirmed Monday that he had admitted to several hacks, including leaking footage of the long-awaited video game, and would subsequently face a public trial.

According to recent reports, U.K. authorities confirmed earlier reporting that Kurtaj hacked several companies, including while he was confined to a hotel amid police protection from rival criminal gangs. The authorities said Kurtaj used an Amazon Fire TV stick to hack the companies, which breached his bail conditions.

Sources indicate that both Buchanan and Kurtaj were members of overlapping cybercriminal groups, dubbed 0ktapus, Lapsus$, and later Scattered Spider. These prolific hacking gangs mostly consist of teenagers and young male adults, lending to the term “advanced persistent teenagers,” whose focus and motivations were to steal as much money as possible through various cyberattacks.

Over the years, the hackers were collectively responsible for hundreds of cyberattacks targeting big companies, including Coinbase, DoorDash, Mailchimp, and Nvidia.

By late 2024, both U.K. and U.S. authorities say they had indicted five of the hackers whom they believed were key members of the hacking groups, including Buchanan. The U.S. Department of Justice stated this week that Buchanan is the fifth and final defendant to be sentenced in this case.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sony might be attempting to patch jailbreak vulnerabilities before the biggest game of the year introduces.
  • According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto VI fans will have to download a new PlayStation 5 update, or they won't be able to launch the game.
  • As IGN reports, PS5 firmware patch 14.23 is 1.267GB in size and contains "security fixes to the system software." Sony didn't say why it's required to run GTA VI on the PS5.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sony might be attempting to patch jailbreak vulnerabilities before the biggest game of the year introduces.

According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto VI fans will have to download a new PlayStation 5 update, or they won't be able to launch the game. Sony has released new firmware for the console that's required to access the long-awaited title. It's encouraging fans on X to download and install it before the game's release at midnight on November 19, so they don't have to wait a second longer to start playing.

As IGN reports, PS5 firmware patch 14.23 is 1.267GB in size and contains "security fixes to the system software." Sony didn't say why it's required to run GTA VI on the PS5. However, IGN notes that it was released just a day after a famous PS5 jailbreaker claimed they were able to successfully dump a game binary on PS5 firmware version 14.22. Presumably, that means they were able to extract and copy data from a disc or a digital version of a PS5 game. Firmware 14.23 may have patched whatever allowed them to do so.

Those planning to get the game sometime today may want to purchase and install it soon. The digital version is 212GB in size and would take more than an hour to download for those with a 1Gbps internet connection. Rockstar Games has also rolled out pre-release patches since GTA VI became available for pre-order, with the latest one being 600 MB. The patches should automatically download for those who've already preloaded the game.

Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software enhancement that is required before playing Grand Theft Auto VI. Players should download this update prior to midnight on November 19 so that they're ready to play on launch day, November 19.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xiaomi is pushing the limits of modern smartphone specs with a killer design, flush camera lenses, and a next-gen Snapdragon SoC.

If you’re looking for a phone with top-tier specs, Xiaomi has a latest phone for you. The Xiaomi 18 Pro and Xiaomi 18 Pro Max are the firm’s latest flagships, available starting today, November 17. When looking at the spec list for the Xiaomi 18 series, it’s difficult to find anything that was left out.

During the launch presentation, Xiaomi emphasized that its latest privacy display wasn’t just a copy of “other privacy displays.” Rather, they created an entirely new subpixel layout called HyperRGB 2.0 that delivers far higher resolution and brightness output than the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra. You can also enable and disable the privacy display feature on the Xiaomi 18 Pro series with a click of the new AI button on the left side of the phone. Functionally, Xiaomi’s privacy display looks nearly identical to Samsung’s, including the ability to have specific apps use it.

Sources indicate that both models feature identical specs, including the privacy display and cameras, with the exception of the screen size, battery capacity, and charging speed. Here are the differences:.

The 120Hz LTPO display is bordered by a 0.99mm bezel, the smallest in the industry so far, 4,000-nit peak brightness, and TÜV Rheinland Triple Eye Care Certification, including a 2160Hz PWM dimming rate. Inside the phone is a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 processor with a 3D IceLoop cooling system, and each model’s silicon-carbon battery includes 28% silicon content.

Industry observers note that on the back is a pair of 200MP cameras, including a 1/1.28-inch main sensor and a 1/1.56-inch periscope telephoto sensor. These are massive sensors, especially compared to the 1/3.94″ and 1/2.52″ telephoto sensors in the Galaxy S26 Ultra. Despite their size, Xiaomi packs them onto the back in an island with fully flat glass — no protruding camera lenses!

It has been revealed that that island on the back isn’t just for cameras, though. It also packs in a 120Hz LTPO M11 OLED panel with 4,000-nit peak brightness for ultra-high-quality selfies and group shots, plus support for notifications and apps. Xiaomi created a fresh GenAI Apps feature that lets you create your own apps on the back display, plus official support for several popular apps like Google Maps, Spotify, and more.

Sources indicate that the Xiaomi 18 Pro series ships with HyperOS 4 (Android 17) and includes 3 months of Google AI Pro, plus 5TB of Google Cloud storage. The Xiaomi 18 Pro retails for €1399 for the model with 12GB RAM and 256GB storage, or €1599 for 12GB/512GB. The Xiaomi 18 Pro Max starts at €1599 for 12GB/256GB, €1799 for 12GB/512GB, and a 16GB/1TB model will be available soon for €2099.

It has been revealed that some retailers also sell a bundle that includes the Official silicone magnetic case, which usually retails for €39, as well as the Magnetic Remote Stand, which retails for €69. That remote stand functions as a MagSafe-style stand and remote, giving you camera shutter functionality and a scrolling feature.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Oura developed a tool for its frequent-flying members that could help them stave off the worst of jet lag.

Ahead of the busy holiday travel season, on Tuesday, Oura confirmed Jet Lag Plan, a newly introduced feature designed to help travelers feel alert and energized after crossing several time zones.

Also: Oura Ring users may get in-app access to real doctors soon – what we know.

Jet Lag Strategy takes into account your travel itinerary, sleep patterns, and body responses to provide guidance for traveling members entering new time zones.

Jet lag happens when circadian rhythms are at odds with local time zones, but there are a few things people can do to adjust.

Oura factors in the direction of travel, how many time zones are crossed, individual light windows, and sleep timing.

Ring owners will enter their flight details, including information like multi-stop trips, and also include the reason for the trip. Oura adjusts the Jet Lag Plan accordingly, and a business trip’s plan may differ in intensity from that of a vacation.

Recent findings suggest that “Two people on the same flight can get different plans, because guidance reflects your itinerary, your typical sleep schedule, and your chronotype,” Oura writes in a blog post. The chronotype refers to Oura’s sleep chronotype, which categorizes owners into six types (early morning, morning, early evening, and so on) based on their historical sleep activity.

Also: I wore the Oura Ring 5 for a month.

Industry observers note that after adding these details, Oura provides each user with timely guidance throughout their trip. This guidance could include recommendations on when to begin or end caffeine consumption or light exposure, and when to start preparing for sleep. The strategy is designed for those crossing three or more time zones. Members can follow along with these recommendations by checking them off as they complete each one. Users can also talk to Oura’s Advisor in the event of flight or timing changes.

Jet Lag Proposal is now available for Oura Members with Oura Ring Gen 3 or later.

It has been revealed that go to your home screen, tap the + and select Jet Lag Plan to get started. You can also tell Oura Advisor about a trip to initiate Jet Lag Plan. If the Oura app detects a time zone shift of 3 or more hours, Jet Lag Plan may appear as a push notification.

In iOS 27, Apple confirmed iPhone Handoff, a networking feature that allows users to switch cell service between two eSIM-enabled iPhones. Text strings in Google’s SIM Manager app suggest the company is preparing a similar feature for compatible Android phones, according to Android Authority.

Recent findings suggest that on Apple’s side, any iPhone in the US running iOS 27 with a T-Mobile or Verizon-provided eSIM can use iPhone Handoff. AT&T does not currently support iPhone Handoff.

However, the code strings uncovered by Android Authority show that Android’s Fast Switch will work similarly to iPhone Handoff, in that consumers must be signed in to both devices under the same Google account for the feature to work.

Strings in Google’s SIM Manager app also point to no sharing between two people, so this feature isn’t a way to circumvent carrier fees by adding service to someone else’s phone for the price of one.

If Fast Switch works anything like iPhone Handoff, which it appears it will, one eSIM can be switched between two phones. So, calls, messages, location services, and other information synced to your Apple ID can remain consistent between two devices.

Also: 5 hidden iOS 27 features that make older iPhones better.

Some third-party apps, like banking, communications, or social media, may also remain consistent across the two phones, depending on the app’s syncing behavior.

Features like Apple’s iPhone Handoff and Google’s Fast Switch are ideal for people who regularly use two phones. Business owners and digital creators may want one phone strictly for business purposes and the other for personal use.

Also: Google Wallet turns your Android phone into a digital house key.

In a recent development, in that case, one person can keep up with two phones without paying for two phone service lines through their carrier. Still, users will incur a fee, as T-Mobile charges $5/month for iPhone Handoff, while Verizon charges $10/month.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that archive of Our Own (AO3) is back up, finally ending its lengthy outage after over two weeks.
  • According to recent reports, non-profit parent organisation the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) revealed AO3's triumphant return on Sunday, Nov.
  • Now AO3 has woken up, and while some features have been temporarily disabled to get the website back up more swiftly, OTW states that no data was lost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that archive of Our Own (AO3) is back up, finally ending its lengthy outage after over two weeks. The Hugo Award-winning fanfiction website went down due to a security incident late last month, and was expected to take up to four weeks to return. Fortunately it didn't take quite so long, with owners now taking to social media to celebrate AO3's revival.

According to recent reports, non-profit parent organisation the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) revealed AO3's triumphant return on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 3:00 a.m. ET / 12:00 a.m. PT, almost exactly 17 days since it first confirmed the outage on Oct. 29 at 3:13 a.m. ET / 12:13 PT. This was also a mere day after the website turned 17, users having lamented that AO3 spent its birthday "in a coma.".

Now AO3 has woken up, and while some features have been temporarily disabled to get the website back up more swiftly, OTW states that no data was lost.

"Your works, bookmarks, kudos, etc., are still safe," OTW remarked in its upgrade announcing AO3's return.

It has been revealed that AO3's return is exciting news for millions of people. The internet went through a multi-fandom meltdown during the AO3 outage, which Forbes previously described as "the gold standard of fanfiction sites." Fanfiction-deprived fans took to sharing saved stories among themselves, while some even flocked to Tumblr for their fandom fix.

As such, the news of AO3's recovery swiftly spread, with some fanfiction readers rushing to spread the word on social media like Paul Revere on his midnight ride.

While many in the U.S. woke up to the news of AO3's recovery, others found out while otherwise going about their day. Attendees of a Yves concert in Melbourne, Australia learned of the development after X user @Alyssa_Aroha held up her phone in the crowd to display the words, "AO3 IS BACK UP." Video of this has since gone viral, racking up over 1.1 million views on X, with attendees reportedly having screamed and cheered at the news.

@Alyssa_Aroha herself found out about AO3's return from X, quickly telling her friend before holding up her now viral sign.

"I go to a lot of K-pop concerts and people like to hold up signs to make the crowd cheer while waiting," @Alyssa_Aroha told Mashable. "I knew the reception in the venue [170 Russel] was bad so I held it up. No-one saw at first till my friend laughed and took a photo, then someone else yelled in surprise and suddenly EVERYONE was taking videos and photos with flash and cheering...

In a recent development, "Fan spaces are so vital and it's so lovely that a space that is so accessible for people around the world to share art with each other is so widely beloved. [Also] Yves' concert was incredible.".

Not everybody at the K-pop concert understood the significance of @Alyssa_Aroha's message. Concertgoer and X user @gyublickyy noted that "the dude behind me was a self proclaimed 'the only straight person in a yves concert' and he was going what the hell is ao3." But for many others it was a moment of collective joy and community.

"In the Yves concert, waiting for it to start, and people start screaming so I assume she's come out early," posted @himejoshiorbit. "No. AO3 is back.".

Meanwhile, attendees at Filipino komiks and art market PasKomiket reportedly learned of AO3's return from organisers who announced it over their PA system. The news prompted cheers from the crowd, many of whom immediately attempted to access the website on their phones.

Fortunately, fans have largely been understanding and patient, with many simply happy that AO3 is back. OTW has stated that its volunteers are continuing to work on restoring AO3's functionality, and will provide further updates as they come.

It has been revealed that AO3 celebrated 11 million registered users in June, though it's likely that an even higher number of people missed it while it was down. AO3 only requires registration for publishing fanfiction, not reading it, OTW having reported that AO3 received an average of around 108 million daily page views in 2025.

UPDATE: Nov. 17, 2026, 12:14 p.m. AEDT This article has been updated with comment from @Alyssa_Aroha.

Have you been using the newly introduced Siri AI? If so, how much? I’ve been turning to it a lot since the release of iOS 27. Well, how we use it — and how often — will soon depend on how much we pay for an iCloud+ blueprint.

Also: 5 apps I need Siri AI to work with now that it’s open to third-party developers.

Recent findings suggest that apple hasn’t been shy about stating that the use of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence for specific tasks would face daily access limits. Increased limits would be granted based on your iCloud+ subscription. Now the company has revealed how much it will cost you and when the limits will begin.

It has been revealed that “Starting with the 2027 software releases, Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are available for free for owners with a supported device set to a supported language,” Apple mentioned on a support page updated November 16. “Some features rely on powerful server models and have limits where increased access is available with eligible iCloud+ looks, starting with the 27.3 release.”.

iOS 27.3 is expected to launch in early December, so that’s when the daily usage limits will kick in.

At that point, people with no paid iCloud+ blueprint and even those with the $0.99-per-month 50 GB plan will be the most limited, with Apple saying only that they’ll face a “Standard Device Limit.”.

Sources indicate that what is a standard limit? That depends not just on how many times you tap into Siri per day but on what tasks you assign it. Basic Siri commands, such as setting timers and alarms or sending standard text messages, will remain free and unlimited.

Also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

Advanced Siri and Apple Intelligence tasks will bump into the usage limits. These include the following, according to Apple:.

Sources indicate that one positive here is that the limits are per device not per account. That means you can use Siri AI and Apple Intelligence with the same account across your iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Vision Pro without fear of chewing up too much of your quota.

Sources indicate that this all sounds like a way for Apple to steer people to more expensive iCloud+ accounts. But the limits are in place for a key reason. Basic commands are processed on your device, so they don’t require the use of Apple servers. More advanced tasks are processed using server-side AI models, which can feel the strain if too many people access them all at once.

Also: What you’ll pay for AI agents will be wildly variable and unpredictable.

How will you know if you use up your daily allotment and what happens then? You’ll receive a notification if you hit your limit for a particular feature category. At that point, you can still give Siri basic tasks to perform. But advanced ones will be paused until your limit resets the next day. Otherwise, Apple is undoubtedly hoping that people who continually run into limits will upgrade to a pricier iCloud+ blueprint.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Who knew one of the most delightful responses to the incessant wave of AI slop would be a DIY fish tank game?

In a recent development, developed by Kaleb Lechowski aka byKaleb, Drawquarium is a sweet new cozy sandbox game out on Steam that's essentially the bloomscrolling of video games. Since the trailer dropped, the game's been dubbed "anti-AI" and has seen commenters on YouTube and X delighted with the game's handcrafted feel — the "brb crying because of a fish game trailer" responses are accurate.

Sources indicate that and according to the Lechowski's Steam description, the game is not for you if you "want action or excitement. No combat, no explosions. Think of Drawquarium as the opposite of GTA 😄.".

The premise of Drawquarium is simple: draw a fish, name it, and watch it come to life swimming in your own digital aquarium. The game is focused on unlocking your creativity and sense of lighthearted tomfoolery, as you can either use templates or come up with your own ungodly creations. Reader, I'm loving my octopus sick:.

Recent findings suggest that in his Steam notes, Lechowski describes why he, a 3D artist in the film industry, made Drawquarium: "My heart kept pulling me toward a small, very personal game idea. One of the reasons I started developing this game was that I wanted to bring my children’s drawings to life 💖." Can't argue with that.

In a recent development, first, you'll need to title your aquarium, then it's time to draw your first fish and name them. I tend toward themes for sandbox games — shout out to my Gilmore Girls-themed faction in Cult of the Lamb — so I've named my creatures after sea goddesses.

Drawquarium's easel mode feels like a supercharged, thoughtful, fun version of MS Paint, with advanced digital brushes and tools that easily help you craft a fish-like being — and reader, when you accidentally fill the screen with the Paint Bucket instead of one section, there's an undo button. Drawing my first fish, I took more time than I thought, adding stripes and fins and flourishes to my little Amphitrite. Once you're happy with your undersea creature, click "give me my fish" and you'll drop your little creation into the tank.

Sources indicate that watching your work – be it a marine masterpiece or a passable abstract – swim around the tank is deeply satisfying. The fish spawn as tiny wee sea bairns and grow in size (something you can also set).

It has been revealed that once your fish is settled, you're instantly prompted to draw them a friend, which takes you back to the creative drawing board. You can clone the fish, start again, or if you need an idea, the lightbulb at the top of the easel will give you suggestions like "draw a steampunk fish," or "draw a fish reading the newspaper." You can unlock templates as you go, and the various photo editing tools you're used to are here: clone and replicate, mirroring, and erasing.

Of course, this is a drawing game, so you don't have to contain your creativity to sea creatures like I did (but my turtle slaps). Maybe your fish look like hats, stereos, or butts, all swimming in your own cursed little fish bowl. You do you, buttfish.

According to recent reports, decorating your tank with plants is next, as you can sketch out plants of a wild and wonderful nature. My one tip here is to play with the opacity and brush size settings, as you can create some satisfying tendrils of varying texture. And in a sweet feature, when it comes time to feed your fish with a click, it's also up to you to draw their meal. I know it's not ideal to feed octopus babies cupcakes but this is my aquarium, my choice of fish food.

You'll need to clean the tank floor (the fish instinctively run from the vacuum), and you can gather coins from the tank to buy more templates — at this stage, the game doesn't have real in-game transactions.

According to recent reports, once you've become thoroughly locked in to making latest types of deep sea residents, there's a wallpaper mode which pops your aquarium onto your desktop so you can sit with your creations all day. This is the real magic of the game, bringing your painstakingly crafted (or slapdash) efforts into your everyday routine.

Sources indicate that in week after week, month after month, of news about how AI is eating creatives' lunch, Drawquarium is a quietly triumphant achievement. A stunning use of human creativity in a deeply relaxing, cosy sandbox game, it's a refreshing treat.

Drawquarium is out on Steam (and as Creative Bloq points out, make sure you're buying the official game, as copies have popped up).

Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO shook up the AI market and US economy last week, but now via The Wall Street Journal Huang has spoken out publicly for the first time since stepping down, and he signals he’s ready to return as CEO if asked.

Today Robbie Whelan at The Wall Street Journal published Jensen Huang’s first public statement since departing Nvidia last week.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said in a short statement. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”.

Home Depot isn’t hiring for the festive season?

The timing is likely no coincidence, as Nvidia is set to report its quarterly earnings later today.

In a recent development, even though Huang technically resigned as CEO rather than being fired, it was clear that his ouster wasn’t exactly his choice. Thus, today’s statement is the former CEO formally putting it out into the world that he’s ready to return if asked.

Since Huang stepped down, President Trump publicly called on Apple’s Tim Cook to step in as Nvidia CEO. But it’s expected that a new CEO—assuming it’s not Huang—will take much longer for the company to find and Cook is unlikely to want the job.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s new Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector in my tests.

Because Notebooks are built with the sources you provide, like textbooks, files, or notes, the sites are created with the data that is in your Gemini Notebook. Notebook has three tabs: Sources, Chat, and Studio. The site option is in the Studio tab, listed under what you can create.

If you’re taking a college class, you could put all the information you need to prepare for a test and use the interactive site as a study guide that you can share with others.

To test this, I gave Notebook the following prompt:.

“Make me a site that visually explains how cellular respiration works, breaking down each stage with interactive diagrams and self-check flashcards.”.

Since I’m not in a class that would give me those study materials, I gave Gemini online sources to use for this. Gemini cited the sources in my notebook, then spent a few minutes creating the interactive site. Gemini will give you a quick update when it’s done, including a summary of the source information as it pertains to your request and instructions on where to find the site.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As previewed at I/O 2026, you can text — via Google Messages and iMessage — or email directly with Gemini.

Instead of using the Gemini app, you can now reach the AI assistant to “start tasks and get updates” using your preferred method of communication. To get started, go to gemini.google.com/channels.

You can now assign Gemini ‘tasks’ for free in six countries.

Industry observers note that text with Gemini works via Google Messages and iMessage. Google does note that this method is “not end-to-end encrypted and may be accessible by your carrier.” The setup process involves verifying a phone number. Existing numbers associated with your Google Account appear automatically, and there’s the ability to add a upcoming one.

Afterward, you’ll receive a text from Gemini via RCS Business Messaging that offers a pretty straightforward chat experience. Before sending, booking, or other “major actions,” Gemini will ask for 1-tap confirmation.

Sources indicate that …you can text a request, snap a photo of a school flyer to add dates to your Google Calendar, or get scheduled check-ins in a private 1:1 thread. If your aims change while Gemini is working, simply reply to the text to steer the task mid-run without starting over.

(Amusingly, Text with Gemini coexists with the existing Google Messages integration, which you can distinguish by the old blue/purple icon.).

Email with Gemini lets you “start tasks and get updates by emailing” gemini@google.com. Google explicitly names Gmail, Apple Mail, or Outlook as supported clients, while emails from Gemini are always “1:1 to you (never “Reply-All”) with a link to review and confirm your results.”.

Forward a batch of school emails to add key dates to Google Calendar, spot schedule conflicts, or send over threads and PDFs to sort out medical bills and track insurance renewals.

Recent findings suggest that you can manage phone numbers and turn off both options from this upcoming Channels page. If you’re more familiar with using your email client or phone’s messaging app, Text and Email with Gemini might boost your assistant usage. This is available first in the US.

Meanwhile, when announced in May, these two options were intended for Gemini Spark, which has since been integrated into the main Gemini experience as “tasks.”.

#1217. Tech Report: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI model training – here’s how

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (507 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI model training – here’s how

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (507 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI.
  • Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me.
  • In a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI. But for people with privacy concerns, the only way to opt out of this was to delete your entire chat history. Now, Google is overhauling the process to eliminate that drawback.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me.

In a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI. Here’s how this works now — and how it will work down the road.

Currently, Gemini offers a setting called Keep Activity that controls not only whether and for how long your chats are saved but also whether they’re used to train the AI. You can’t separate the two.

To correct this problem, Google will replace Keep Activity with two new settings. With the first setting, you’ll be able to keep or delete your past chats and choose how long your history will be saved. With the second setting, you’ll be able to decide whether your chats, including all text and attachments, will be used for model training.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

“With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training,” Google mentioned in an announcement shared to Gemini customers via email.

Here’s how this will play out. If your Keep Activity setting is off when this change is made, both fresh settings will be off. If your Keep Activity setting is on, both new settings will be on. That means you’ll need to head to Gemini’s Settings if you wish to opt out of model training but still be able to view and access your previous chats.

In a recent development, almost all AIs include a setting for model training that you typically have to manually disable if you’re concerned about your privacy. But most let you opt out without turning off your chat history.

ChatGPT offers a setting called “Improve the model for everyone,” which is double-speak for model training. But this is easy enough to turn off. Microsoft Copilot provides settings for “Training on conversation activity” and “Training on voice conversations,” both of which you can disable to opt out of model training. Claude’s AI training option is turned off by default. But you can always control this by checking the setting for “Help improve our AI models.”.

Also: 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027.

In all those cases, you still retain access to your conversation history. In contrast, Google has been the only AI player among the majors to impose a restriction for those who want to opt out of AI training. Based on past actions, Google has often earned a reputation for being privacy-unfriendly. I’m glad to see the manufacturer take this step in the right direction.
