💡 Key Takeaways
  • Waymo robotaxis are no longer allowed to operate on California freeways after the state’s Department of Motor Vehicles restricted the Alphabet-owned tech giant’s operations following several incidents that raised safety concerns.
  • Industry observers note that california’s DMV, which regulates the testing and deployment of autonomous vehicles in the state, issued the operational restrictions on Waymo on November 11.
  • The DMV confirmed the newly introduced restrictions to TechCrunch, stating that the department took action after three Waymo autonomous vehicles entered an active construction closure on U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Waymo robotaxis are no longer allowed to operate on California freeways after the state’s Department of Motor Vehicles restricted the Alphabet-owned tech giant’s operations following several incidents that raised safety concerns.

Industry observers note that california’s DMV, which regulates the testing and deployment of autonomous vehicles in the state, issued the operational restrictions on Waymo on November 11. However, the restrictions weren’t made public until Tuesday. San Francisco Business Times was the first to report the order.

The DMV confirmed the newly introduced restrictions to TechCrunch, stating that the department took action after three Waymo autonomous vehicles entered an active construction closure on U.S. Route 101 near Burlingame, and another separate incident involving California Highway Patrol vehicles on Highway 280 in San Francisco.

Waymo has complied and is preventing its robotaxis from accessing freeways in any of the markets it operates in, including those outside of California. Waymo currently has commercial operations in 15 U.S. cities.

The DMV said Waymo’s freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety.

“The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present, despite a prior restriction and corrective actions implemented following similar incidents that occurred on May 18, 2026,” according to an emailed statement sent to TechCrunch.

The DMV mentioned the restrictions will remain in place until Waymo can demonstrate that it has taken “effective corrective actions” to address the deficiencies.

Waymo spokesperson Dana Gallagher told TechCrunch the company has temporarily restricted freeway operations across its other operating markets to evaluate its performance.

Industry observers note that “Safety is at the foundation of everything we do,” Gallagher said in a statement. “Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”.

Waymo began offering freeway rides in late 2025, a commercial milestone that has been central to its expansion in major metro areas. Freeway access allows Waymo to connect riders to airports and other destinations more efficiently, slashing travel times by avoiding slower surface streets.

That has been particularly important in the San Francisco Bay Area because Waymo’s service area stretches from the city south to Silicon Valley. Freeway access has dramatically shortened trips across the Peninsula that previously took 45 minutes or more than an hour.

Recent findings suggest that in May, Waymo abruptly stopped operating on highways. The company didn’t cite a specific reason at the time, but several social media posts highlighted Waymo robotaxis driving through traffic cones and struggling to navigate construction zones.

Waymo robotaxis returned to freeways in July after the company remarked it updated the self-driving software system to improve performance around freeway construction zones.

#1124. Ways to tell if someone blocked your phone number on iPhone

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (606 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Ways to tell if someone blocked your phone number on iPhone

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A missing read receipt or an unanswered FaceTime call could mean a block, or it could just be a bad signal.
  • Let's be very clear about this — if someone has blocked your phone number, whether on iPhone or Android, that's their right and you shouldn't disregard it.
  • That noted, there's no inherent harm in trying to determine if you've been blocked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A missing read receipt or an unanswered FaceTime call could mean a block, or it could just be a bad signal.

Let's be very clear about this — if someone has blocked your phone number, whether on iPhone or Android, that's their right and you shouldn't disregard it. They probably don't want to talk to you, and deliberately trying to circumvent that could constitute harassment, maybe even at the criminal level. It's better to just move on.

That noted, there's no inherent harm in trying to determine if you've been blocked. It may even be crucial if you have an honest reason to think it was a mistake. While blocking a number by accident is unlikely, it's not impossible.

Since you're using an iPhone, the clues are mostly in Apple's Phone, Messages, and FaceTime apps. But you may want to expand your sleuthing to third-party messaging platforms, depending on how you previously communicated with someone.

In a recent development, your biggest clue is likely to be a call in the Phone app that goes straight to voicemail after one ring or no ring at all. You can only be sure after multiple calls at varying hours, however. That's because with a single call, or several calls within a short timeframe, there may be alternative explanations. Perhaps the person has Do Not Disturb or another Focus mode on. It could also be that their cellular or Wi-Fi signal is bad, that their phone is off or even that they're in the middle of an iOS or Android enhancement, which requires a lengthy reboot.

Recent findings suggest that A faster way of confirming things is by calling from a second number if you have one, such as Google Voice or a work phone. Exercise caution here, since this could be seen as harassment. Passive options are always preferable. Besides, if someone knows (or knew) you well enough, there's a good chance they've blocked all your normal contact options.

Sources indicate that further signs that you've been blocked could include FaceTime calls failing to connect, or absent read receipts in the Messages app even though it's been hours or days since your last text. Once again, there may be other complications at play. Apart from bad signal quality or a phone being turned off, if they're an iPhone owner, it could be that they've disabled iMessage, or that Apple's servers are temporarily offline. Android phones won't provide receipts at all unless they're using RCS instead of SMS.

Sources indicate that while third-party apps like WhatsApp, Signal and Telegram are often linked to your phone number, blocking someone via iOS settings doesn't affect those apps, for the simple reason that they rely on frameworks beyond Apple's control. Missing read receipts or unanswered calls could be evidence that you've been blocked across multiple platforms. However, they might mean something else, such as Meta or Telegram experiencing technical difficulties.

You also can't read too much into automated replies, regardless of the app. They can, however, be used as a kind of "soft" block, discouraging you from calling or texting without seeming so harsh. If you're encountering an iPhone's automatic call screening when it wasn't there before, the other person may have deleted you from their Contacts app, which could make it the most obvious sign that you should stop.

In a recent development, unfortunately, that's about for your options. Apple and your carrier can't tell you that you're blocked. That would be unethical anyway, since it would violate the privacy of the blocker. You're just going to have to rely on all the clues we've suggested so far.

#1122. Breaking: I’ve Used VSCO’s Lightroom Rival Desktop Editor and It’s Great for Creatives

Breaking: I’ve Used VSCO’s Lightroom Rival Desktop Editor and It’s Great for Creatives

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (601 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • VSCO is best known these days for its iPhone and Android editing app that makes pics look all cool and analog.
  • The desktop app will be immediately familiar to any photographer who’s spent any time in Lightroom or Capture One.
  • VSCO’s wide range of color presets has always been where it shines the brightest.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VSCO is best known these days for its iPhone and Android editing app that makes pics look all cool and analog. But the tech giant is launching its first stand-alone desktop photo editor for Mac, called VSCO Studio Pro, bringing its famous filmic presets—and a wealth of editing tools. I’ve used it, and while it’s not yet my sole image-editing solution, it’s great for getting those dreamy vintage vibes out of your photos.

The desktop app will be immediately familiar to any photographer who’s spent any time in Lightroom or Capture One. There are exposure, contrast, highlight, and shadow sliders along with color sliders for white balance or individual color adjustments. It’s par for the course for any raw image editor.

VSCO’s wide range of color presets has always been where it shines the brightest. Numbering just north of 200, Studio Pro packs in all the presets, from color classics like the organization’s A1-10 range to a wealth of black-and-white options and a host of presets designed to emulate real film stocks like Kodak Gold or Fuji Velvia. VSCO says these are modeled on real scans of these film stocks to make them as authentic as possible.

In a recent development, it’s the presets that I love the most in VSCO’s app. Years ago, the company sold its presets as a downloadable Lightroom preset pack, which I have used in my photography workflow almost daily for the past 13 years, and their look is identical here. While it hasn’t sold the Lightroom preset pack in about a decade, VSCO’s Studio Pro app finally lets photographers achieve those same looks in desktop editing.

It has been revealed that with Studio Pro, VSCO clearly has its sights on Lightroom. While Adobe is increasingly filling its services with various generative AI tools that radically alter your image’s content, VSCO is taking a more stripped-back approach that focuses on the creative side of color and exposure adjustments.

According to recent reports, it’s still quite bare-bones at launch, with several features I need for my own photography missing, like masking. I can’t make selective edits to my images—like using a gradient to tone down the highlights only in the sky. Apparently this is coming soon, as are bloom and halation tools, which are already in the app, but grayed out with a “soon” marker next to them. Ditto the spot removal tool for cleaning up dust or sensor spots.

The significant thing for me, though, comes down to cataloging and archiving of my images. I have several terabytes of images cataloged in my Lightroom library, available to edit on any device I sign in on — including phone, tablet or desktop. While VSCO will have some basic organization options within the Studio Pro app (grouping images into “Projects”—again, coming soon), it’s not as full-featured as Lightroom’s archiving system. I worry that once I’m working with thousands of images across multiple photoshoots, things will swiftly become cluttered and difficult to navigate. Time will tell.

I don’t imagine VSCO’s app will necessarily be the first choice for working pros who need strict cataloging, backups and remote access. I count myself in that category, and for me Lightroom’s cloud storage remains the biggest reason to stay with Adobe, while others swear by Capture One for its Sessions-based filing system and its tethered shooting workflow.

By contrast, I see VSCO Studio Pro appealing more to enthusiast photographers who want to efficiently add real creative flair to their images and don’t necessarily want to spend on the commercial tools, cloud storage, or AI options offered by Adobe.

Nvidia’s Q3 revenue has more than doubled, with income from data centers up 110 percent from last year, to $107.6 billion.

Nvidia’s Q3 revenue has more than doubled, with income from data centers up 110 percent from last year, to $107.6 billion.

Recent findings suggest that interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress declared the company’s Q3 earnings on Tuesday, without initially mentioning former CEO Jensen Huang or the details of his departure, or possible attempt at a return. On the earnings call accompanying the release, board chair Harvey Jones kicked things off by saying the board “does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO,” and that “we will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation,” before Kress started with her comments on the results.

Industry observers note that as it predicted in the last financial update, Nvidia is now on the list of companies that have pulled in over $100 billion in a single quarter, with revenues of $115.8 billion, up 103 percent from the same period last year and higher than its expectation of $108 billion. This quarter’s figures include data center revenues of $107.6 billion, which were up 110 percent, and edge computing (which includes the consumer gaming PC business and devices like the new RTX Spark laptops) revenue of $8.2 billion, up 42 percent.

The organization reported $65.3 billion in profit, a newly introduced record.

In a recent development, “Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” noted Colette Kress, interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of NVIDIA. “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater.”.

In the fourth quarter, Nvidia expects revenues of $130 billion.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ambience’s new tools suggest tasks for each shift and flag barriers to discharge.

Ambience Healthcare has added Rounding Assistant and Discharge Readiness to its hospital AI software, to help care teams prioritise tasks and spot barriers to discharge earlier. The manufacturer also points to customer results on billing, including a 6.5% rise in case mix index at Onvida Health.

Sources indicate that ambience Healthcare has added two AI tools that help hospital teams decide what to do next for each patient, the company confirmed on Tuesday. They join its existing software, which writes clinical notes and suggests billing codes for hospital stays.

Rounding Assistant pulls together overnight events, changes in a patient’s condition and a list of suggested tasks for each shift. Discharge Readiness flags medical, practical and social problems that could delay a patient going home, earlier in the stay.

Ambience is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins and the OpenAI Startup Fund. It counts Cleveland Clinic and Mayo Clinic among its customers, and ties its fees to results. Cleveland Clinic has also backed Dyania, another hospital AI startup.

Much of the pitch is about money. Ambience aims to raise hospitals’ case mix index, a measure of how sick patients are that helps set what insurers pay. At Onvida Health, discharges handled with Ambience scored 6.5% higher than a year earlier, the tech giant says.

“To justify the investment, we needed roughly a 1.5% improvement in case mix index,” said Mike Lewis, chief financial officer of Onvida Medical Group.

Lewis said Onvida’s own finance team checked the results. Ambience also indicates admission notes written with its tool captured 59% more of the diagnoses used in quality rankings, in one health system’s review of 1,100 stays. None of the figures come from independent research.

According to recent reports, AI note tools are still under scrutiny. In August, England’s patient watchdog warned that AI scribes were getting drug names and diagnoses wrong. Rivals are growing fast too: Heidi raised $340M in September, and Google rolled out Gemini for healthcare last week.

#1117. “Trump was in bed with Jensen”: Critics balk at Huang’s wish to return to Nvidia

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1986 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

“Trump was in bed with Jensen”: Critics balk at Huang’s wish to return to Nvidia

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1986 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On Monday, large trucks began circling the streets of Washington, DC, carrying billboards urging Congress to investigate the Trump administration’s ties with Nvidia’s disgraced CEO Jensen Huang.
  • In a recent development, “Jensen was in bed with a spy from China,” the billboards created by the Tech Oversight Project (TOP) alleged.
  • According to recent reports, right now, Trump is supporting a campaign to bring back Huang as Nvidia’s CEO—despite many Republicans calling it a “horrible idea.” Breaking his silence, Huang issued a statement Tuesday saying he would be “honored” to return, but the board noted reinstatement is not under consideration as an internal investigation into US spying claims remains ongoing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Monday, large trucks began circling the streets of Washington, DC, carrying billboards urging Congress to investigate the Trump administration’s ties with Nvidia’s disgraced CEO Jensen Huang.

In a recent development, “Jensen was in bed with a spy from China,” the billboards created by the Tech Oversight Project (TOP) alleged. “Trump was in bed with Jensen.” TOP is a nonprofit that describes itself as “dedicated to reining in Massive Tech.”.

According to recent reports, right now, Trump is supporting a campaign to bring back Huang as Nvidia’s CEO—despite many Republicans calling it a “horrible idea.” Breaking his silence, Huang issued a statement Tuesday saying he would be “honored” to return, but the board noted reinstatement is not under consideration as an internal investigation into US spying claims remains ongoing. Huang used the moment to say that his interests align with the US’s, saying:.

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. Nvidia has been my life’s work. Building it into the manufacturer it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like Nvidia be possible. I love our country, and I love Nvidia.

Trump may have learned as early as this spring that Huang was potentially the target of Chinese espionage, but the president claimed recently that he didn’t know Huang was potentially exposed to a Chinese spy as he was becoming a prominent part of Trump’s inner circle, CNN reported.

If Trump wasn’t adequately briefed, it raises question about whether the White House acted with “sufficient urgency” to address a serious espionage threat, CNN mentioned. But if Trump is deflecting, an even “graver question” will emerge about why Trump didn’t act on information and instead continued to keep Huang close, CNN said.

Instead of distancing himself from the Nvidia CEO, Trump invited Huang to sit at the head table during a state dinner with China’s president Xi Jinping, and last month, Trump awarded Huang the National Medal of Science, the nation’s highest scientiﬁc honor, for his AI achievements.

Industry observers note that “Not only has he continued to do nothing, he’s invited that very CEO into the White House and on state visits to China with him,” Sacha Haworth, TOP’s founder and CEO, told Ars. “And the question we all have to ask is ‘why on Earth would he do that?’”.

What Trump and Nvidia knew—and when—have become central questions for some Republicans, as well as top Democrats who initiative to investigate the scandal when they assume control of key committees in Congress next year. Andrew Yoon, head of research for a nonprofit called CivAI, which warns the public of dangers from AI, told Ars that Huang doesn’t need to be compromised by China to have endangered the US. Prioritizing boosting profits over national security alone is “pretty concerning.”.

In a recent development, “I think the most notable thing here is that Jensen Huang has been at the absolute forefront of lobbying to be able to sell chips to China,” Yoon said. “He has leveraged his very deep relationships with government, especially President Trump, in order to be able to sell as many Nvidia chips to China as he can get away with. If he could be selling Blackwell chips to China, I’m sure he would be.”.

It has been revealed that yoon noted that evidence suggests some Chinese AI models have been trained on Blackwell chips. Even with China’s push to prioritize domestic chipmakers like Huawei, Nvidia chips remain “indispensable” to China’s frontier AI goals, Yoon remarked. And national security experts fear that access to high-end chips will help China advance its military AI or gain economic ground.

Sources indicate that the White House isn’t commenting on Trump’s relationship with Huang. Among the lawmakers accusing the Trump administration of “corruption” is Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), The Wall Street Journal reported. He has already asked the White House to “preserve all communications” between Trump and Huang.

Sources indicate that other lawmakers are “seeking more information about what Trump knew about the relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang,” the former Megaspeed CEO whom Huang admitted to having an affair with. They also want to know more about “the administration’s failure to stop artiﬁcial-intelligence chips from going to China,” WSJ reported, and Nvidia’s reportedly $25 million donation to the White House ballroom.

According to recent reports, “It is not just an intelligence matter; it’s also a potential corruption issue,” Blumenthal said. “There needs to be a really penetrating, comprehensive investigation of all the possible compromises of our intelligence that may have occurred, but also… that Donald Trump is so high on the head of Nvidia, and now is potentially linked to intelligence compromises.”.

Trump has profited off Nvidia’s success while in office, buying “millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares in his personal brokerage accounts since returning to oﬃce in 2025,” the WSJ reported. The White House maintains that the president has no role in managing his stock portfolio.

Recent findings suggest that other officials advising Trump on AI also benefited from relaxing export curbs, TOP said. On Tuesday, the group issued a report summarizing what the public knows about potential conflicts of interest of two Trump officials: former White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

Haworth, TOP’s founder, told Ars she’s concerned that Sacks and Lutnick abused their power to convince Trump to let Nvidia sell cutting-edge technology to China, while standing to “gain astronomical amounts of money.”.

In a recent development, “The public is outraged by Nvidia’s CEO for compromising our national security, but we didn’t get here because of Jensen Huang’s missteps alone,” Haworth noted. If “Nvidia was knowingly doing business with companies tied to illegal chip sales and smuggling with China,” then “the Trump administration was asleep at the wheel,” she said.

“White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick were protecting their own fortunes rather than looking out for Americans,” Haworth stated.

If the US fails to hold them accountable for alleged conflicts of interest, “it would send a signal that powerful men once again cannot be held to account and that powerful men are protecting powerful men,” Haworth said.

Sources indicate that detailing Sacks’ alleged conflicts, the group cited Fresh York Times reporting that the former AI czar had long supported Huang’s stance that allowing Nvidia to sell more chips in China would help the US stay ahead in the AI race. After Sacks became Trump’s key AI advisor, Huang quickly forged a “tight bond” with him, and “both stood to benefit” from their push to sell chips to China, TOP reported.

Recent findings suggest that also notably, while advising the White House, Sacks opposed policies such as the Trump administration’s recent move to cut off China’s remote access to US-made chips through now-restricted Southeast Asian data centers. Citing Sacks’ alignment with Huang, TOP reported that after just one meeting with the two men, Trump decided to allow Nvidia to sell AI chips to China that the Biden administration had previously blocked.

Industry observers note that huang valued his alliance with Sacks, TOP noted, citing reporting that demonstrated Huang declaring last year that Nvidia was “lucky” to have Sacks advising Trump. But TOP is concerned that the alliance was built on mutual financial interest and that Sacks took a part-time role in the Trump administration to avoid divestments or disclosure requirements that might have revealed the extent of his possible conflicts of interest.

It has been revealed that TOP flagged two areas it believes warrant Congressional investigation. While advising Trump to embrace AI deregulation, Sacks and his firm, Craft Ventures, continued investing substantially in AI. Sacks also stood to benefit from pushing Trump to integrate AI into warfare and national security tools, TOP’s report noted. Craft Ventures has invested in Palantir, “a Peter Thiel-founded government contractor seen as a ‘rising star’ in the US Defense Tech World and holding hundreds of millions in US government defense contracts,” TOP said.

Even within the Trump administration, officials have turned on Commerce Secretary Lutnick, seemingly looking to blame him for mishandling the Nvidia spying investigation and allowing Trump to maintain close ties with Huang despite apparent intelligence risks.

In a recent development, lutnick has bragged publicly that he promised Huang “really easy access to the President” after joining the administration, TOP reported. That alliance helped push Trump to approve the sale of Nvidia H200s to China, TOP said. And that seemed to directly benefit Lutnick, TOP said, because before he was confirmed as secretary, he was CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald, which held $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock.

“In his role as Secretary, Lutnick is responsible for policing exports of sensitive technology to adversaries and global rivals, like China,” TOP reported. “Lutnick and the tech giant he controls benefited greatly from opening sales of Nvidia chips to China.”.

After Lutnick was required to hand that company over to his son, Cantor Fitzgerald “maintained extensive commercial ties to Nvidia, helping arrange billions of dollars in financing for companies in its AI business universe and repeatedly hosting its top executives,” TOP noted.

Those investments shifted substantially around the same time that Lutnick began facing pressure to “crack down on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company suspected of funneling Nvidia’s advanced artificial intelligence chips to China,” TOP reported. Cantor Fitzgerald “reduced its Nvidia holdings by nearly 50 percent between September 2025 and March 2026,” TOP said.

However, when Trump was reportedly first told of the spying allegations this spring, Cantor Fitzgerald again continued to boost Nvidia. Most prominently, the firm helped “finance the expansion of one of Nvidia’s newest business partners, IREN,” facilitating a five-year, $3.4 billion deal between Nvidia and the Australia-based cloud computing provider.

Industry observers note that among those now criticizing Lutnick for weak enforcement of export controls that appeared designed to protect Huang’s bottom line is Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. But even with scrutiny coming from within the Trump administration, not everyone is convinced that Lutnick did anything wrong. Yoon suggested that, given Lutnick’s long career, there may be normal explanations for potential financial conflicts.

“Maybe a separate question is ‘should people with a long storied history in business and industry be working in government at this level?’” Yoon noted.

Haworth remarked the next 48 hours will be critical in determining whether Huang succeeds in returning to Nvidia.

“I think it’s going to be incumbent on the incoming Democratic leadership to insist that whether or not he returns, investigations will follow,” Haworth mentioned.

But Yoon thinks Nvidia is unlikely to bring Huang back any time soon, despite current evidence suggesting that “Nvidia’s actions here have been perfectly legal” and that “influencing a political system for your financial interests is very much legal in the United States.”.

It seems “untenable for Nvidia to continue doing what they’re doing,” Yoon stated. Zooming out even more, he suggested the scandal indicated that the entire AI industry can no longer afford to operate under a profit motive alone, so long as governments continue positioning the technology as a strategic asset.

If US investigations expose corruption, bribery, treason, or other crimes, Nvidia risks losing some of its dominant stake in the GPU market. On Tuesday, The Information reported that some Nvidia customers had already lost trust and were looking to Google and AMD for more stability.

Nvidia has also been accused of intervening in a Commerce investigation, which Yoon said could also be “pretty consequential” if any evidence bears that out.

It has been revealed that “I think it’s pretty unlikely that Huang makes it back to Nvidia any time soon,” Yoon stated. “Maybe he goes on a redemption tour and comes back in five years or something, but I’m not really seeing a path forward for him right now.”.

As AI tools have gotten better at transforming videos, social media creators have faced a growing wave of accounts copying their work. From influencers watching their videos reappear with a different face, to comedians finding their jokes delivered by fictional performers, the copies can preserve the original creator's material while sending the attention elsewhere. (Read Mashable's feature on this phenomenon here.).

Now, Instagram is introducing tools to help creators catch those copies and decide what happens next.

In a recent development, on Tuesday, Nov. 17, Instagram head Adam Mosseri declared that the platform is beginning to roll out "Content Protection," as a "fresh way to see and review copies of your own videos in your insights on Instagram," giving creators the choice whether to hide them or add a link back to the original. Separately, Instagram is testing a way to detect stolen scripts and jokes, even when someone uses AI to change the visuals.

In a recent development, "We will not get everything right at first, but we’ll keep improving as fast as we can. More to come," he wrote on Threads.

Recent findings suggest that for now, the feature remains a limited test with a small number of creators, a Meta spokesperson told The Hollywood Reporter, with prepares to expand access. The distinction matters for creators whose work has been repackaged this way, especially comedians like Sarah Purdum, who told Mashable in October that her material had been used by an AI account.

It has been revealed that purdum also said that the comedy community had been discussing similar experiences, particularly among women. Other female comedians like Olivia Carter and Julia Jasunas, also had material appear in videos featuring AI performers.

Another account, "Tiffany Sloane," (account now disabled), posted a version of a routine by comedian George Brett Olson that also copied elements of his appearance and performance. Olson shared a side-by-side comparison showing similar outfits and gestures alongside the same joke. The account's Instagram highlights also linked to an OnlyFans page.

Industry observers note that the broader Content Protection rollout gives eligible creators a way to respond when Instagram finds visual matches of their original videos. The tool specifically "alerts eligible creators when it finds visual matches of their original videos and lets them decide what happens next, including tracking a copy, adding a credit link or hiding it," a Meta spokesperson told THR.

To enroll, eligible creators will receive an invitation to enroll in their activity feed. Once enrolled, their new original videos are protected automatically, and they can manually select eligible older videos for protection.

The full extent of the disruption isn’t known yet.

It has been revealed that A variety of Apple services, including iCloud, the App Store and Apple Pay, appear to be down in an apparent outage that has affected much of the firm's online infrastructure. According to Downdetector, a handful of people began reporting connection complications around 11:30AM ET, before the number of outage reports jumped to the thousands around 12:29PM.

According to recent reports, as of 2:34PM ET, Apple's System Status page currently lists a number of ongoing challenges. It says iCloud account sign in "may be slow or unavailable," and that AppleCare on device is "temporarily unavailable" for all users. The Simple Trick That Keeps Poached Eggs Perfectly Intact

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (935 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Poaching eggs takes practice, but even the gentlest drop into a simmering (never rolling) pot of water can yield sloppy results.
  • One simple, no-fuss step is all that stands between you and perfect poached eggs, according to a bona fide egg expert I spoke with—and then validated with my not-so-scientific at-home test.
  • According to recent reports, lisa Steele is a fifth-generation chicken keeper and author of Fresh Eggs Daily and In Season: 125+ Sweet and Savory Recipes Celebrating Simple, Fresh Ingredients.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Poaching eggs takes practice, but even the gentlest drop into a simmering (never rolling) pot of water can yield sloppy results. It turns out the reason your poached eggs look less like the neat, tidy protein puff you see on food magazine covers and more like a Jackson Pollock has to do with the egg’s structure, not your kitchen skills.

One simple, no-fuss step is all that stands between you and perfect poached eggs, according to a bona fide egg expert I spoke with—and then validated with my not-so-scientific at-home test.

According to recent reports, lisa Steele is a fifth-generation chicken keeper and author of Fresh Eggs Daily and In Season: 125+ Sweet and Savory Recipes Celebrating Simple, Fresh Ingredients. She talked me through the single, foolproof step that makes stovetop egg poaching dead simple.

Picture it: a pot full of water, maybe with a dash of distilled vinegar, at the gentlest simmer so you don’t subject your delicate egg to a tornado of activity when you submerge it. You painstakingly crack the egg into a shallow bowl first and carefully slip it into the pot. Regardless of your good intentions, the egg then clouds the water and turns all wispy, like some sort of blond dementor.

Recent findings suggest that you haven’t done anything wrong here; you’ve just failed to understand an egg’s basic structure. “There are actually two components of the egg white, or albumen,” Steele explains. “There’s the thicker part of the white which encases the yolk, and then there’s a separate, thinner layer of egg white around that. It’s the thinner part of the egg white that will spread and turn wispy when you drop an egg into the water.”.

The thing is, you can easily get rid of the thin, watery white part of your egg using one simple tool you’ve probably got in a drawer somewhere and about a minute of your time. Set a small mesh strainer over a cup or bowl, crack the egg into it, and wait.

“Straining an egg removes the thinner whites that likely won’t adhere to the rest of the egg and result in shaggy, wispy threads,” Steele says. “It won’t affect the flavor outcome of your poached egg, but it is purely for appearance’s sake.” (And potentially your sanity’s or sense of accomplishment’s sake, I might add.).

While the egg’s flavor stays unchanged, for Benedict lovers, straining the egg first slightly improves the white-to-yolk ratio in the poached result and makes the texture more consistent, while also creating a tidy, photogenic package.

Once your raw egg is in the strainer, you may notice nothing happens right away, and you may feel the urge to move the egg around a bit to get things going. But don’t zhush, which threatens to scramble the egg. Simply wait for gravity to do its thing; it takes about a minute. It’s akin to what happens when separating whites from yolks, except here you’re separating whites from whites.

In a recent development, “Let the thin part of the egg white drip down into the bowl,” Steele claims, “then gently slide the egg into the simmering water.” The strainer can also serve as a handy vessel for transferring the egg, especially if you’re making only one. If you’re doing multiple eggs and don’t want to risk cooking any remaining white onto the mesh by submerging it, place the strained egg in a small, shallow bowl as usual before easing it into the water. Without the thin, watery white part, you’ll notice a discernible textural difference in the egg even when raw.

The straining step alone can almost completely change your poached egg game in an instant, but for the best results, follow the best poaching protocol. You don’t want a full pot of water at a rolling boil like you would for pasta. “Fill a pot or saucepan with a few inches of water and bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to low so the water is just barely simmering with small bubbles floating to the surface,” Steele advises.

According to recent reports, creating a little whirlpool will further help your remaining egg white stay snug. “Using a wooden spoon or silicone spatula, swirl the water, then gently slide the egg into the center of the whirlpool as you keep swirling for another few seconds around the egg until the egg white turns milky and starts to set up around the yolk,” Steele says. “At this point, you can push the egg to one side, add another egg into the center and repeat the process.”.

A soft-poached egg takes about three minutes, and because you’ve removed the watery part of the egg white, you’ll get a nice firm structure to hold the still-runny yolk — the poached egg ideal.

In a recent development, since poaching is a delicate process, no matter your fresh straining habit and how strictly you follow the recommended procedure, “using the freshest eggs possible is very crucial when you are poaching because the egg white gets even more thin and watery as the egg ages,” Steele states. “The membrane holding the yolk together also weakens, making the yolk more susceptible to breaking.” So if you don’t have them on hand already, get yourself a strainer and some fresh eggs and put this newfound tidbit to the personal test.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, was Google feeling a little left out of the recent wave of tech outages?
  • It has been revealed that as it turns out, the manufacturer was trying to head off reports of a Gmail outage that began circulating on X on Tuesday around the same time that Apple was seeing a number of verified outages of its own.
  • The concerns seemed to stem from an X post by Downdetector, a crowdsourced website where users can report service disruptions themselves and see if others are having problems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, was Google feeling a little left out of the recent wave of tech outages? The company took to X on Tuesday to announce that its Gmail service is actually running just fine. In a post, the company stated it was not right now seeing evidence of a broad Gmail service disruption and reminded people they could always check Gmail’s real-time status on its online dashboard.

It has been revealed that as it turns out, the manufacturer was trying to head off reports of a Gmail outage that began circulating on X on Tuesday around the same time that Apple was seeing a number of verified outages of its own. While some posts on the social network suggested Gmail was experiencing a disruption, others said they were not having any problems.

The concerns seemed to stem from an X post by Downdetector, a crowdsourced website where users can report service disruptions themselves and see if others are having problems. Downdetector is not an official source for verifying or understanding the true scope of internet outages, and as people become more concerned about possible cyberattacks, the site’s data may become less valuable over time if every minor glitch and hiccup is reported as an “outage” by non-technical users.

The fact that Google had to announce it was not having an outage speaks to the growing anxiety around the reliability of major tech services. Over the past week, Apple and Microsoft experienced outages, an FAA network failure led to a nationwide ground stop, and some banks and airlines also reported disruptions.

However, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on Fox Business Network’s “The Claman Countdown” on Tuesday that the U.S. is not at the moment facing coordinated cyberattacks. He told the outlet, “We do not see the indicia of a coordinated cyberattack — let me just be clear about that — and we do not see the indicia of state-sponsored activity here.”.

Instead, Clayton attributed the rise in problems to businesses patching their systems. The patching may be a downstream effect of AI, as newer models have become increasingly adept at uncovering previously unknown vulnerabilities. “They’re upgrading them, they’re putting patches in place,” he remarked, adding that this is happening at “a much larger scale” than before.

As a result, some of the systems are “not coming back as expected in all cases,” he added.

Breaking: Is IONIX the best-kept secret in cybersecurity?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (847 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As organizations expand their digital infrastructure, their external attack surfaces are becoming increasingly difficult to secure.
  • According to recent reports, the result is a shrinking window for defenders.
  • IONIX has built its approach around this challenge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As organizations expand their digital infrastructure, their external attack surfaces are becoming increasingly difficult to secure. Cloud environments, third-party vendors, subsidiaries, web applications and AI services introduce new potential entry points. At the same time, AI is accelerating how swiftly attackers can discover vulnerabilities, identify exposed assets and turn weaknesses into opportunities for exploitation.

According to recent reports, the result is a shrinking window for defenders. IONIX argues that the likelihood of an individual exposure being exploited has shifted dramatically. It has moved from a historically low probability (statistically safe by default) to approaching a default-breach scenario. While the exact risk varies by vulnerability and environment, the broader point is clear. Maintaining a complete inventory and validating exposures continuously are becoming essential security requirements.

IONIX has built its approach around this challenge. Through its External Exposure Management Platform, the company combines autonomous asset discovery, continuous security assessment, exploitability validation and agentic remediation. Its central premise is that if attackers operate at machine speed, defenders need to do the same.

Industry observers note that enterprise attack surfaces rarely stop at the boundaries of internally managed infrastructure. Vendors, cloud providers, subsidiaries and acquired businesses can introduce internet-facing assets that remain outside traditional security monitoring.

Industry observers note that IONIX addresses this visibility gap through autonomous discovery that maps external assets, vendor-managed infrastructure and digital dependencies. The firm says its platform discovers 30% to 50% more assets than competing approaches. This helps organizations identify shadow IT, overlooked applications and third-party exposures.

In a recent development, through its Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM) capabilities, IONIX aims to continuously discover, monitor and prioritize exposures across an organization’s external environment. This broader visibility becomes increasingly crucial as enterprises adopt new technologies and expand their digital supply chains.

It has been revealed that identifying vulnerabilities is only part of the problem. Traditional security assessments can generate extensive findings, but not every concern represents an immediate or exploitable threat.

IONIX combines continuous security testing with non-disruptive active exploitability validation to distinguish actual exposures from theoretical risks. Its Exposure Validation capabilities examine vulnerabilities, misconfigurations and exposed technologies, testing whether identified weaknesses represent genuine security risks.

Industry observers note that the platform then prioritizes findings according to severity, exploitability, potential blast radius and asset importance. The objective is to help security teams concentrate on exposures that present meaningful business risks rather than working through undifferentiated vulnerability lists.

IONIX is also extending exposure management beyond continuous discovery and assessment through its Live Exposure Defense solution.

Industry observers note that the technology addresses a particularly urgent challenge: what happens when a upcoming vulnerability is publicly disclosed? Instead of requiring security teams to manually determine which systems might be affected, IONIX automatically ingests newly published CVEs. It then correlates them against its mapped external attack surface.

It has been revealed that the platform then uses agentic analysis to identify potentially affected assets, validate actual exploitability through safe, non-intrusive testing. It also recommends concrete mitigation measures. IONIX targets a 12-hour window from public CVE disclosure to validated exposure and actionable mitigation.

Industry observers note that for confirmed exploitable web assets, this can include generating specific remediation workflows and mitigating actions. Specifically, it can generate Web Application Firewall (WAF) rules through supported providers such as Akamai and Cloudflare. The approach gives security teams a practical mitigation path rather than another vulnerability alert to investigate.

Recent findings suggest that IONIX’s approach has attracted interest from organizations managing complex digital environments. These include Warner Music Group, BlackRock, Infosys, the Telegraph, E.ON and Grand Canyon Education.

John Remo, former SVP of Global Cloud, Infrastructure and Cybersecurity at Warner Music Group, described the platform as delivering almost immediate value without adding pressure to technical staffing. Mike Manrod, CISO at Grand Canyon Education, highlighted its ability to provide a dynamic view of an organization’s external attack surface from an attacker’s perspective.

Sources indicate that these examples reflect a broader consideration for enterprise security buyers. The value of exposure management is not simply how many vulnerabilities a platform discovers, but whether it helps organizations understand and reduce their actual risk.

The cybersecurity market is crowded with platforms promising better visibility and vulnerability management. IONIX is pursuing a more integrated approach, bringing asset discovery, exploitability validation, risk prioritization and agentic mitigation into one continuous process.

Industry observers note that its focus on digital dependencies and machine-speed response addresses a growing challenge for enterprises. That challenge is keeping security controls aligned with an attack surface that never stops changing.

As AI accelerates both the discovery and exploitation of vulnerabilities, organizations will have less room to rely on incomplete inventories and periodic assessments. IONIX is betting that continuous visibility, validated exposure and faster mitigation will become fundamental requirements for the next generation of enterprise security.

#1106. What exactly are Flock cameras and how can you spot one?

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (753 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

What exactly are Flock cameras and how can you spot one?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Flock cameras are everywhere, and they’re easier to miss than you think.
  • According to recent reports, basic descriptions of Flock cameras fall woefully short of their true capabilities and potential uses.
  • In truth, there are more than a dozen manufacturers and vendors of ALPRs; their products just aren't called Flock cameras, and each has its own aesthetic characteristics.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Flock cameras are everywhere, and they’re easier to miss than you think.

According to recent reports, basic descriptions of Flock cameras fall woefully short of their true capabilities and potential uses. Most people are familiar with the automated license plate reader (ALPR) version, usually pole-mounted and paired with a solar panel. If that were all there was to it, this would be a very short article. But Flock Safety (Flock Group Inc.) has become deeply intertwined with the defining terminology of ALPR cameras.

In truth, there are more than a dozen manufacturers and vendors of ALPRs; their products just aren't called Flock cameras, and each has its own aesthetic characteristics. For all intents and purposes, however, they are identical. If you see Motorola on the side of one, it likely does much of what a Flock does: read plates and log vehicles.

According to recent reports, most are vertically oval, narrow in width and fairly small, roughly the size of your hand. They're designed to capture your license plate and the time and place you passed by. Most are also accompanied by a solar panel. Leonardo and Genetec make the most visually distinct versions. Leonardo's are blockier, rectangular in shape, with some elongated versions. Genetec's are horizontally oval, with the same narrow width as Flock's variations, only flipped. Motorola manufactures a mix of the two.

The problem is that some Flock cameras can easily be mistaken for a standard traffic camera and vice versa. Because of this, it's difficult to accept the absolute accuracy of a project like DeFlock, which uses volunteers to identify Flock cameras visually. There's no centralized or formal verification system to independently confirm the sightings.

It has been revealed that flock also sells more than ALPRs. Depending on what the customer wants, the system can log details like roof racks on cars and bumper stickers. Some setups have microphones and others can recognize things like clothes and beards.

Flock cameras usually turn up where traffic funnels. They're often mounted on poles at intersections and busy traffic areas. Since many homeowners associations (HOAs) are major Flock camera customers, it shouldn't be a surprise to find them at neighborhood entrances. Shopping centers aren't off the list of potential locations either. The aesthetics aren't irrelevant, but since several manufacturers make them, there are a few other telltale signs to look for as well.

Flock cameras are meant to capture license plates, so look at where they're aimed. Check for Flock's bird logo on the camera and a solar panel above it. Because most are self-powered, there's usually little to no additional equipment nearby. Red light and speed cameras are typically larger and wired to traffic signals or enforcement poles. White, elongated cameras are another lookalike, but they mostly help traffic signals adjust to traffic flow. Some states also mount signs next to speed cameras so they're easy to identify.

Sources indicate that keep in mind that there are other variations of Flock cameras out there. The Flock Condor is a mounted sphere that rotates 360 degrees and tracks people. Naturally, these are mounted near areas with heavy pedestrian traffic. Flock also makes a mobile security trailer, a gunshot detector and a drone-as-first-responder. Because companies are using video integration tools to convert standard IP cameras into plate readers, it will be increasingly difficult to identify Flock or Flock-type cameras.

Recent findings suggest that as a rule of thumb, if it's pointed at you, it's potentially watching you. But for a broader view, check the Atlas of Surveillance, a searchable database from the Electronic Frontier Foundation that shows what technology law enforcement agencies use. Search your town or county to see whether police are using plate readers.

Sources indicate that while some services like MapQuest can help you find Flock cameras in your neighborhood, be wary of crowdsourced maps. DeFlock uses OpenStreetMap data collected from volunteers, but there's no official public list, so a missing pin doesn't mean there isn't a Flock camera sitting there.

In a recent development, pins can also be wrong, since it's easy to confuse a Flock camera with the countless security and traffic camera variations. A Flock camera doesn't have to belong to a public agency. Flock and Flock competitors also sell to HOAs and retailers.

If you want to find every Flock camera in your city, county or state, you have to put in the work. Submit a public records request, attend the next city council meeting or ask your HOA and local businesses.

  • It indeed appears there have been an unusually high number of outages recently.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that microsoft 365, including Outlook, goes down for two days starting on Nov. 12. The FAA grounds all U.S. flights due to an air traffic control telecommunications problem on Nov. 13. Chase bank suffers an outage due to a software issue on Nov. 16. Later that same day, United Airlines' website goes down, affecting all departing flights. On Nov. 17, an internal update issue disrupted some of Apple's services.

Major companies and services appear to be experiencing outages all at the same time. Conspiracy theories surrounding these events are spreading, and people are asking what in the world is going on with all these recent outages — and are they connected?

It indeed appears there have been an unusually high number of outages recently.

Recent findings suggest that "Compared with the past 12 months, the past week has been unusually busy," Ookla's Lead Industry Analyst Luke Kehoe stated in a statement provided to Mashable. "Americans sent nearly 6 million reports in the past seven days to November 16, more than in any other week over that period, and the number of services with problems flagged on Downdetector was higher than in all but a few weeks.".

According to Ookla, the two-day Microsoft 365 outage was the largest reported downtime issue on Downdetector "since the AWS outage of October 2025, with 3.9 million US reports in the 60 hours after it began.".

However, the reason it feels like outages have occurred more frequently is that the affected companies have been fairly large.

Recent findings suggest that as Kehoe explains, the data shows what "appears to be a cluster of big events." More people are reporting problems because the services suffering from outages have larger user bases. There have been numerous periods with more widespread outages, but among services with smaller user bases.

So, what about the timing of all these substantial system failures? Has AI turned into Skynet, wreaking havoc across the web? Is a hacker collective responsible for the outages? Are they indeed connected? The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile Products available for purchase through affiliate links. If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Industry observers note that the answer, as uneventful as it may seem, is no. They are not connected, per se, at least not in the conspiratorial sense. And while investigations are still ongoing into some of these major outages, it does seem that they are, for the most part, isolated internal incidents.

It has been revealed that however, there are reasons why it appears major technology networks are more vulnerable to outages lately. And, they are somewhat connected, however, it's in a not so nefarious way.

“When major organizations and critical services experience disruptions in close succession, it can create the impression that the incidents are connected, but that isn’t necessarily the case," Shane Buckley, CEO of cloud security tech giant Gigamon, told Mashable in a statement.

"Organizations today operate within a highly interconnected ecosystem of applications, networks, cloud infrastructure and third-party services," Buckley explained. "A failure in one part of that ecosystem can have downstream effects across multiple services, while unrelated technical concerns can also surface at roughly the same time. Until the root causes are confirmed, it’s notable not to assume these incidents are connected.".

It has been revealed that basically, many essential services in the tech industry have consolidated into just a few major providers. As a result, many companies depend on the same service providers for their online platforms. If that service provider goes down, multiple platforms that depend on it will go down with it.

Sources indicate that for example, many online companies use Cloudflare to manage their traffic and ensure maximum uptime. However, when Cloudflare went down last year, many platforms that depend on the service suffered downtime issues along with it. This happened even though those individual companies' systems were not experiencing any problems.

Recent findings suggest that another example of how many systems are dependent on one another is the Chase online banking outage from just this past Monday. Consumers initially reported that multiple financial institutions were suffering from outages, including services like Zelle. It turns out, only Chase was suffering from concerns. But, because customers at other banks and financial services were experiencing issues when trying to transfer money to Chase accounts, it gave off the perception that there were wider problems with online banking systems.

Recent findings suggest that so, as I noted, nothing nefarious here. It's just the normal, everyday consolidation of essential online services into the hands of just a few major conglomerates. No need to worry!

Sources indicate that there's no question the PS5 has handed the Xbox Series X and S their collective rear ends from a sales perspective this console generation. That's a shame for Microsoft fans. Even though there are drawbacks you should understand before buying an Xbox Series X, for my money, it's still an excellent console. It's also one that supports a rich suite of accessibility options, as does its little sibling. One of the biggest? Fairly robust keyboard and mouse support.

Industry observers note that using traditional PC peripherals on a console might seem a bit outfield, but hey, the Dreamcast was doing it a quarter of a century ago, so there's definite precedent. There are actually a ton of Xbox games that offer at least partial mouse and keyboard support. Let's get into the mouse and keyboard options that should work with the Xbox Series X/S, and also discuss how to set them up. Plus, we'll examine just how many games support non-gamepad control schemes on Microsoft's current-gen consoles.

You sure can... but there are caveats. While Microsoft has done a commendable job at providing accessibility features for Xbox fans, mouse and keyboard support on Xbox Series X/S isn't universal across all games. Additionally, of the titles that do work with PC-based peripherals, not all of them offer native support. That means certain actions in non-native titles will require you to have a controller nearby to progress.

Sources indicate that there are more restrictions, too. There's presently no way to connect a Bluetooth mouse or keyboard to either Xbox Series console. For those looking to hook up their favorite PC gizmos, you're looking at either wired peripherals or ones that come with 2.4GHz dongles.

Industry observers note that that's slightly annoying. The best Xbox Series X/S accessories are generally wireless because you're likely sitting a decent distance away from your TV while playing your favorite games. Unless you keep your Xbox at a desk like a PC, wired mice and keyboards are probably out of the question for everyday living room play. Dongles it is, then.

Oh, and there's one more catch. You can't use a mouse to navigate around the Xbox dashboard, which is a bit of a bummer.

It has been revealed that setting up a keyboard and mouse on an Xbox Series X/S is relatively simple, but functionality beyond that is going to vary based on the specific game. The easiest and most practical way to get started with PC peripherals on your Xbox is to plug in a wireless keyboard dongle and a mouse dongle: You can use the two USB-A slots on the back of either console, or the one at the front.

From there, you can utilize the keyboard for typing on the Xbox dashboard (though as previously mentioned, mouse navigation is a no-go). Once you launch a game, things are a tad up in the air. The title may recognize your PC-style peripherals immediately, and you can start pointing and clicking. Or, you may well need your trusty Xbox controller to navigate into the settings menu, where you should be able to select mouse and keyboard inputs, if the title supports them. Microsoft provides the platform, but accessibility options are up to the individual developer, so this workflow will vary game to game.

Basically, prepare to always have your gamepad in reach if you want to use typical PC peripherals with an Xbox Series console. Just in case.

It has been revealed that A surprising amount. We're not quite talking PC levels here, but the list of Xbox games with current mouse and keyboard support (as reported by Pure Xbox) shouldn't be sniffed at by WASD fans. Well over 100 titles feature levels of mouse and keyboard functionality at present, though native support isn't guaranteed in all of them. That means you'll occasionally have to break out your Xbox controller to navigate menus. If you hop on the Xbox Store, a game's listing page should tell you what level of mouse and keyboard support a title offers. Those that don't natively offer traditional PC controls will be marked as "Limited.".

In a recent development, looking for a few big hitters that support native mouse and keyboard controls on Xbox Series X/S? You'll find Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, Halo Infinite and Gears of War: E-Day. Considering one of those games demands complex simulation controls that never quite felt at home on a pad, and the other two involve landing headshots on alien beasties from afar, mouse and keyboard sounds like a great way to experience all three. I always thought Master Chief's 2021 open world was overly criticized, and now I'm eager to replay it on Xbox, sniping hordes of Brutes with my favorite mouse, the Inphic F9 Mecha.

Recent findings suggest that there are also competitive shooters like Overwatch that support cross-platform play, and will automatically pair you with fellow mouse and keyboard users if the game detects a PC-style control scheme on console. After all, in a fast-paced online shooter, bringing a gamepad to a mouse-and-keyboard match is like wielding a pillow in a lightsaber battle.

There are a number of benefits to using desktop peripherals with an Xbox Series X/S. Some aren't all that sexy — oooh, I can type my custom license plate in Forza Horizon 6 a teeny bit quicker — but others have far more practical use cases.

According to recent reports, for simulation or strategy games with multiple mechanical layers and rich inventory systems, mouse and keyboard inputs are simply superior. I've had great experiences with these devices on my Xbox Series X playing Jurassic World Evolution 3, even though the dino-park management title does work pretty well with a controller. Keyboard support also gives you more quick buttons to assign should an Xbox title support it, which can definitely be useful in games that involve heavy inventory management, like Cyberpunk 2077.

The main reason you want keys and a mouse, though? For fans of first-person shooters, gamepads can never come close to the accuracy of blasting bullets with the utter precision of a mouse. Halo Infinite, Overwatch, the Call of Duty series and S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl are all well-situated for mouse and keyboard play, among many other headshot-heavy games.

#1101. Latest Update: The World Didn’t End on Nov. 17, but Some Tech Chaos Did Go Down

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1494 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: The World Didn’t End on Nov. 17, but Some Tech Chaos Did Go Down

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1494 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As global conspiracy theories go, this was a juicy one.
  • ET, the Federal Emergency Management Agency and the Federal Communications Commission conducted a test of the Emergency Alert System.
  • In a recent development, the good news: The world didn’t break at that time despite fears.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As global conspiracy theories go, this was a juicy one.

On Tuesday, Nov. 17, at around 2:20 p.m. ET, the Federal Emergency Management Agency and the Federal Communications Commission conducted a test of the Emergency Alert System. That’s when all hell was supposed to break loose. At least, that’s what you might have believed if you only relied on social media.

In a recent development, the good news: The world didn’t break at that time despite fears. The bad news: Some troubling activity did, in fact, happen, even if it may have been unrelated or the result of opportunistic hackers taking advantage of the anxiety. Attackers targeted hundreds of websites with malware seeking to hijack data from credit card transactions, Apple software or cryptocurrency transactions. Sites affected included CNN, IKEA, Fox News and Zoom.

Recent findings suggest that apple and Google also experienced concerns on Tuesday, but it’s unclear if those are related to the hacking that affected websites. Apple’s System Status page reported outages of App Store, Apple Music and iCloud services among others, while some Google owners reported issues with their email.

Coming just days after an abrupt and disruptive government-ordered shutdown of air travel in the US and technical issues that caused an unwelcome outage of widely used Microsoft workplace software, the hacking and the government’s alert test happened in an atmosphere of heightened anxiety.

In a recent development, videos across Facebook, Instagram and TikTok floated the theory that this emergency test signals a catastrophe was coming, potentially stemming from a cyberattack or a digital disruption that could knock out electricity, internet and other services. Many scrambled to buy emergency supplies, pointing to the need for a 90-day stockpile of food, water, cash and essential medicines in case hackers wipe out bank accounts and shut down the web.

Similar rumors spread globally, as the governments of France, the UK and Canada have put renewed attention on the importance of households being able to survive a potential weather-related crisis or technological disaster.

How extreme did the conspiracy theories get? Some cited a 2023 Simpsons episode as proof, which referenced a massive Nov. 17 blackout in Lisa’s future, even though it didn’t mention a year.

For Gen Xers and Boomers, this panic could feel familiar. Leading up to the year 2000, there were fears that a potential computer-related disaster, known as Y2K, would cause widespread chaos and disruption, based on the belief that older digital systems couldn’t handle the calendar change. The fresh year ended with only minor glitches, thanks to a significant global effort to revision computer systems to avoid the bug.

It has been revealed that before we delve into the suspicions, let’s start with a bit of debunking: CNET spoke with multiple experts in disaster preparedness and cyberattacks, who all cautioned against letting our guard down, no matter what the date. But remember that no federal agency or institution has mentioned a blackout.

Recent findings suggest that richard Mariano, a protective intelligence expert at Kronus Intelligence, who spent nearly three decades with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, noted that people share all sorts of things that get picked up and go viral. “Then it creates panic where panic is not necessary,” he said.

Sources indicate that mariano said too many people are spreading fear rather than seeking the truth. “On every one of these social media posts that is suspect or has some form of conspiratorial edge to them: source it, source it, source it.”.

In a recent development, the Emergency Alert System message scheduled for Nov. 17 was similar to the public tests Americans have experienced since 1963, (PDF) when the Emergency Broadcast System replaced an older radio-based warning system called CONELRAD. In 1997, the Emergency Broadcast System was replaced by the EAS, part of FEMA’s Integrated Public Alert and Warning System, which broadcasts emergency alerts to any wireless device in the country, including phones, radios and televisions. The system was designed for the president to communicate with US households within 10 minutes of a national emergency.

It has been revealed that the Nov. 17 test consisted of a nationwide EAS message issued by FEMA, noting that no public action is required. The test included standard alert tones to support accessibility for those who are deaf or hard of hearing and lasted about a minute. This time around, wireless emergency alerts were not triggered on mobile phones. After the alert, programming resumed as normal on TV, radio and other broadcast channels.

Many equate the emergency system with threats of nuclear war, but it could also be used to alert people to a major weather event, a national cyberattack or even AMBER alerts at the local level (without a presidential message). So it’s natural there might be some anxiety.

“With this event simulating an activation of an emergency notification system, it would be a logical next step to worry about what happens if something bad happens during that test,” noted Robby Winchester, chief global professional services officer at SpecterOps, a Virginia-based security organization,.

But, all in all, these system tests are routine. Local stations conduct a weekly test, and federal law requires a nationwide EAS test every three years. In addition to helping people get used to responding to alerts, the tests also allow the government to identify potential technical or operational complications it needs to fix before an actual emergency alert.

Representatives from the FCC and FEMA did not respond to a request for comment.

In a recent development, another factor that helped spark conspiracy theories was a Pentagon order requiring military bases to stock enough supplies for 90 days without outside support. Dubbed “Fortress America,” the initiative memo (PDF) was released in late September but got more attention as the November date approached.

It has been revealed that the timing of that memo coincided with the UK launching a campaign on Oct. 22 called Be Ready, urging citizens to keep enough supplies (PDF) such as water, food, medical kits and pet products to last at least three days. Other countries, including Japan, Sweden and about a dozen more, are also urging citizens to prepare for emergencies.

Still, the blackout rumor isn’t solely driven by government communications. Heightened global instability over the past few months has also played a major role. Just in the last month, the Federal Aviation Administration called a nationwide ground stop on all departing flights; a major Microsoft Outlook outage kept millions of people from working; PHP vulnerabilities exposed websites to hacking; and cyberattacks have targeted supermarket fridges and freezers across Europe.

It has been revealed that on the financial side, Nvidia’s CEO scandal led to a stock plunge and fears of an AI bust, while Paraguay just experienced a major digital bank collapse that froze millions of accounts. The ongoing wars in Iran and Ukraine have sparked national security concerns, and floods in Nepal and fires in Indonesia demonstrate the increased dangers of climate change.

Though there’s never been a nationwide power outage in the US (several regional outages have been triggered by overloaded lines and software bugs), The Fresh York Times reports that there’s still no comprehensive plan for what to do if the country goes completely dark.

It has been revealed that all the online chatter surrounding Nov. 17 raised concerns that warnings of a potential cyberattack might inadvertently trigger one.

It has been revealed that winchester said that even though there’s no specific information indicating an imminent crisis, “it is common for attackers to use current events of all types to help with achieving successful attacks.” The upside? If people are being spurred by government notices and their anxiety over global instability to prepare emergency supplies, it could actually help in the event of a real threat or disaster.

Industry observers note that regardless of whether you bought into the Nov. 17 conspiracy theories, it doesn’t hurt to have some supplies on hand, which could be useful in the event of a digital disruption or weather event, even if it doesn’t involve nuclear weapons or hackers.

“We live in a world where there are many threats to our communities, our families and ourselves,” said Philip Farina, chief advisor for Risky Business and a federal law enforcement veteran. “Understanding the basics of self-reliance is important. Even preparing for a residential fire, which is very common, can help to save lives and protect us better.”.

According to recent reports, you don’t need to buy enough for 90 days off the grid (and most of us can’t afford that), but it’s recommended that families have at least three days’ worth of food and supplies. Some of the basics listed on Ready.gov’s Build a Kit page include:.

While warnings from governments can spark panic and distrust, they can be beneficial at a time when we’re so reliant on the internet and cell service, which can be easily disrupted. Mariano stated it’s worth being prepared in the “old-fashioned ways.”.
